## Ownership

`schema` owns resource definitions. `client/datafn` owns the client storage and sync runtime. `client/runtime` owns browser infrastructure such as account transport, network authority, connectivity, and diagnostic logging. `client/features` owns capability implementations. `client/products` composes those capabilities into product experiences. `client/ui` is the permanent domain-free `@21n/ui` package. `elements` owns atomic controls and UI-only types. `compositions` owns domain-neutral compound UI intended for present or future reuse, including charts, maps, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, file presentation, keyboard listeners, duration inputs, scroll containers, and time selectors. `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, and `branding` owns pure visual brand assets. Package-wide portable platform state belongs to `environment`, while dependency-inversion contracts shared across controls and compositions belong to `hosts`. A single current consumer does not make a composition feature-owned. `client/shell` (`@nucleum/shell`) owns the concrete product shell: navigation, panels, split views, tabs, trails, overlays, modal chrome, and the extension-support layers. `client/surfaces` (`@nucleum/surfaces`) owns cross-feature product surfaces: account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, the command surface (`commandBar`, `commands`, `search`), and `library` resource browsing. `client/application` retains the composition root (`composition/resource-hosts.ts`, `composition/shortcuts.config.ts`), the base/user application layers, modal orchestration, chrome integration adapters, and product-aware branding adapters. Markdown editing and tags belong to memory; combinations belong to spaces. Product-independent shared client behavior lives in the `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace under explicit `app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`, `preferences`, `product`, `resources`, and `shortcuts` owners. Cross-layer billing contracts live in `schema/account`. Keyboard and interaction-mode contracts live in `client/ui/elements/keyboard`; panel and error presentation contracts live in their capability owners. Application wires independently owned implementations into a running product.
It is not the default owner of connected components or workflows.

## Permanent owners

- composition: host registration, product presentation, product shortcut defaults, ordered assembly of owner-defined global and settings commands.
- layers: startup ordering, account access gating, user layout assembly, modal orchestration and telemetry consent/lifecycle wiring.
- chrome: product-connected snippets supplied to the independent shell, including native capture.
- branding: product-identity adapters over portable visual assets.
- paint: product-aware startup presentation and concrete action-component resolution.

The root contains only this charter and the package manifest. New top-level
owners require an explicit architecture decision and checker update.

## Responsibilities owned elsewhere

- shell/navigation and shell/layers: browser navigation, route decoding, platform classes and viewport handling.
- shell/modal: modal chrome and dismissal; application layers choose the concrete content.
- surfaces/library: mixed-resource rendering and bulk selection presentation; features/records owns record actions and bulk mutations.
- surfaces/account: OAuth, session hydration, extension login and environment-change sign-out.
- surfaces/subscription: plan reconciliation and native purchase outcomes.
- surfaces/settings/data-recovery: recovery decisions and UI; persistence/migrations owns headless import mechanics.
- surfaces/settings/about: application-update workflow.
- surfaces/help: documentation, support, connected error recovery and shipped diagnostics.
- surfaces/sharing: permissions and public-link workflows.
- runtime: host detection, native message validation, service workers and log capture.
- shared-state/app-context, preferences and files: application metadata, timezone preferences and native file responses.
- ui/compositions: quick-access grids, hold-action presentation and point-map rendering.
- features/memory/maps: memory popup content and its map adapter.

Application keeps lifecycle sequencing and supplies narrow callbacks to the
owning workflows. Do not move a large layer wholesale into another generic
controller, service, state or utilities directory. Do not add compatibility
re-exports at retired paths.

# `client/shell` — application shell: arrangement and navigation (`@nucleum/shell`)

Charter: how the app is arranged and moved through, independent of what content
fills it. Pure "where things go and how you move", never "what a screen does".

## Owners

`navigation` (URL/history, resource navigation), `topNav`, `bottomNav`,
`leftPanel`, `rightPanel`, `trail`, `layers` (theme, metadata, embed),
`overlays`, `modal`, `paint` (page and
resource resolvers fed through the shared-state action renderer), `split views`,
`tabs`, `sync` and `notifications` chrome.

## Belongs here

Anything that owns URL state, panel arrangement, tab/sidebar behavior, product
menus, or shell events. If removing it would not change what any single screen
does, only how screens are framed and reached, it belongs here.

## Not here

- Domain screens and workflows (account, library, settings, command) ->
  `surfaces/`.
- Portable domain-free UI -> `ui/`.
- Content capabilities -> `features/`.
- Sync scheduling -> `datafn/visibility-sync`; telemetry mechanics ->
  `runtime/telemetry`; consent/lifecycle wiring -> application layers;
  connected support -> `surfaces/help/support`.
- Application composition layers that wire the running product together
  (base/user layers, the action `ComponentResolver`, `AppLoadingView`, and the
  settings action map) -> `application/`.

## Dependency direction (enforced)

Shell is acyclic: it must not import `application/`, `surfaces/`, or
`products/`, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters through
`@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome
(brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status,
capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props provided
by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`).

## Junk-drawer test

A shell component may read navigation and shell state, but it must not contain a
feature workflow. If it orchestrates a domain task (sign-in, billing, resource
browsing), it is a surface, not shell.
# `client/surfaces` — cross-feature product surfaces (`@nucleum/surfaces`)

Charter: user-facing surfaces that are about the app itself or operate across
all content features. Second-order UI: it composes `features/`, `shell/`, and
shared state into product-level experiences.

## Owners

`account` (identity workflows), `subscription` (billing and native purchases), `onboarding`, `help` (docs, support, error recovery and shipped diagnostics),
`settings` (including data recovery), `sharing`, `commandBar` + `commands` + `search` (command surface), `library`
(resource browsing and rendering).

## Why not `features/`

Features are first-order content capabilities a user creates and manages
(memory, focus, collections, spaces, calendar). Surfaces are about the product:
identity, billing, settings, command dispatch, and browsing every resource type.

## Import rules (enforced)

- May import `features`, `shell`, `shared-state`, `runtime`, `datafn`, `ui`,
  and `products`. Application-selected presentation enters through narrow
  shared-state hosts configured before surfaces mount.
- Must not import `application`; this would point a composed surface back at
  its composition root.
- `features/` must never import `surfaces/` — this edge is rejected by
  `npm run check:architecture`.

## Junk-drawer test

- A first-order content capability? -> `features/`.
- Pure arrangement/navigation chrome? -> `shell/`.
- Product wiring (host-contract configuration, base layers)? -> `application`
  composition.
- Dev-only probes and experimental fixtures? -> `tools/`, stories, or delete.
- Shipped troubleshooting actions and diagnostics? -> `help/diagnostics`, preserving their existing access gates.
# `client/features` — user-facing content capabilities (`@nucleum/features`)

Charter: the marquee things a user creates and manages. Each feature is a
self-contained capability reached from outside only through declared entry
points.

## Owners

`calendar`, `collections`, `focus`, `memory`, `records`, `spaces`, `system`.

## Belongs here

A cohesive content capability with its own UI, state, and logic.
`records` owns connected record actions and bulk mutations; shared-state
supplies their headless selection state and application-configured host.

## Import rules (enforced)

- May import `ui`, `shared-state`, `runtime`, `datafn`, and the application
  **shell** surface only.
- May **not** import `products` or application workflows outside the shell.
- Cross-feature imports must target a path declared in
  `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`; there is no barrel.

## Junk-drawer test

If the thing operates *across* features or is *about the app itself* — account
and billing, the command palette, the resource library/browser, settings,
onboarding, help — it is a **product surface** and belongs in the top-level
`client/surfaces/` workspace (see `docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md`).
`features/` must never import `surfaces/`; the checker rejects that edge.

<svelte:options runes={true} />

<script lang="ts">
  import { refreshTimeZone } from "@nucleum/shared-state/preferences/timezone";
  import { performAppUpdateCheck } from "@nucleum/surfaces/settings/about/app-update";
  import { isExtensionEnvironment } from "@21n/shared-utils/browser-environment";
  import { pullForegroundDatafn } from "@nucleum/datafn/visibility-sync";
  import { createLegacyDataRecovery } from "@nucleum/surfaces/settings/data-recovery/legacy-data-recovery.svelte";

  import { refreshAppStaticData } from "@nucleum/shared-state/app-context/app-data";

  import { syncAccountPaidPlanFromExternalProvider } from "@nucleum/surfaces/subscription/plan-sync";
  import { handleNativePurchase } from "@nucleum/surfaces/subscription/native-purchases";
  import { parseNativeMessage } from "@nucleum/client/runtime/embed/native-message";
  import { handleNativeFileMessage } from "@nucleum/shared-state/files/native-file-messages";
  import { initializeUserConfig } from "@nucleum/client/runtime/telemetry/user-identity";

  import "../composition/resource-hosts";
  import type { Snippet } from "svelte";
  import { onDestroy, onMount } from "svelte";
  import { GlobalEvent } from "@nucleum/shared-state/events/event.enum";

  import account from "@nucleum/client/runtime/account/account.store";
  import {
    appLoadingState,
    appStore
  } from "@nucleum/shared-state/app-context/app.store";
  import { userPreferences } from "@nucleum/shared-state/preferences/user-preferences.store";

  import context from "@nucleum/client/runtime/context.store";
  import Diagnostics from "@nucleum/surfaces/help/diagnostics/Diagnostics.svelte";
  import ModalLayer from "./ModalLayer.svelte";
  import AnalyticsLayer from "@nucleum/application/layers/telemetry/AnalyticsLayer.svelte";
  import ShortcutRunner from "@nucleum/shell/shortcuts/ShortcutRunner.svelte";
  import Intercom from "@nucleum/surfaces/help/support/Intercom.svelte";
  import { installVisibilitySync } from "@nucleum/datafn/visibility-sync";
  import { safeRequestIdleCallback } from "@21n/shared-utils/idle-callback";

  import AppLoadingView from "../paint/AppLoadingView.svelte";
  import DynamicMetadataLayer from "@nucleum/shell/layers/DynamicMetadataLayer.svelte";
  import { logger } from "@nucleum/client/runtime/logging/logger";
  import { UserDataMode } from "@nucleum/client/runtime/account/account.type";
  import { getDapId } from "@nucleum/persistence/device-id";
  import PageError from "@nucleum/surfaces/help/errors/PageError.svelte";

  import { uiState } from "@nucleum/shared-state/preferences/ui-state/uiState.store";
  import { Action } from "@nucleum/client/config/action.enum";

  import { embedBridge } from "@nucleum/client/runtime/embed/embed.store";
  import { postMessageToParent } from "@nucleum/client/runtime/embed/embed.utils";
  import { EmbedMessage } from "@nucleum/client/runtime/embed/embedMessage.enum";

  import UserLayout from "./UserLayout.svelte";
  import LegacyLocalDataRecoveryGate from "@nucleum/surfaces/settings/data-recovery/LegacyLocalDataRecoveryGate.svelte";

  import { UIStateScope } from "@nucleum/shared-state/preferences/ui-state/uiState.type";

  import { recentsStore } from "@nucleum/shared-state/resources/recent.store";
  import { resolveProductResources } from "@nucleum/datafn/resource.utils";
  import {
    nucleumDatafnStatus,
    initializeNucleumDatafn,
    reconcileDatafnNow,
    refreshNucleumDatafnStatus
  } from "@nucleum/datafn/datafn.store";

  let {
    children,
    topnav: topnavContent,
    onReady
  }: {
    children?: Snippet;
    topnav?: Snippet;
    onReady?: () => void | Promise<void>;
  } = $props();
  const loadingMessages = {
    cloneUp: {
      message: "Syncing your local data with the cloud...",
      subMessage: "This might take a while."
    },
    pull: {
      message: "Syncing your data from cloud..."
    },
    cloneDown: {
      message: "First login detected. Syncing your data..."
    }
  };
  let loadingMessage = $state<{
    message: string;
    subMessage?: string;
    duration?: number;
    percentage?: number;
  }>({
    message: ""
  });
  let isAppLoading = $state(false);
  let error = $state<string | null>(null);
  let dev_isDisableSyncOnAppear = false;
  let subs: any[] = [];
  let isStartupCompleted = false;
  const recovery = createLegacyDataRecovery({
    initializeDatabase,
    completeApplicationStartup,
    startApplication,
    onLoading: (message) => {
      loadingMessage = message;
    }
  });
  const isDebug = import.meta.env?.DEV;

  $effect(() => {
    if (
      $nucleumDatafnStatus.nucleumMode === "sync" &&
      recovery.isCloudUploadPending
    ) {
      void recovery.uploadPendingCloudData();
    }
  });

  $effect(() => {
    if ($appLoadingState.isBaseLoaded) return installVisibilitySync();
  });

  onMount(async () => {
    postMessageToParent(EmbedMessage.MOUNT);
    if ((<any>window).Intercom)
      (<any>window).Intercom("update", {
        hide_default_launcher: true
      });
    addWindowEventListeners();
    refreshUIStateDerived();
    const uiStateSub = uiState.subscribe(() => {
      refreshUIStateDerived();
    });
    subs.push(uiStateSub);

    const isLegacyRecoveryRequired = await recovery.prepare();
    if (!isLegacyRecoveryRequired) {
      await startApplication();
    }
  });

  function refreshUIStateDerived() {
    const interactionMode = uiState.getState(Action.MODE_OF_INTERACTION, {
      scope: UIStateScope.PRODUCT
    });
    $appStore.interactionMode = interactionMode;
  }

  async function startApplication(options?: {
    isOfflinabilityEnabled?: boolean;
  }) {
    if (isStartupCompleted) return;
    const runtime = await initializeDatabase(options);
    if (runtime) {
      try {
        await completeApplicationStartup();
      } catch (startupError) {
        error = "Unable to initialize local data. Please try again later.";
        logger.error({ at: "startApplication", error: startupError });
      }
    }
  }

  async function completeApplicationStartup() {
    if (isStartupCompleted) return;
    await Promise.all([
      initializeUserConfig(),
      recentsStore.refresh(
        resolveProductResources($appStore.product, "search") ?? []
      )
    ]);
    $appLoadingState.isBaseLoaded = true;
    isStartupCompleted = true;
    if (typeof onReady === "function") {
      await onReady();
    }
    if ($context.isEmbed && $context.isSheet) {
      $appLoadingState.isLocalLoaded = true;
    }
    scheduleIdleMaintenance();
  }

  function scheduleIdleMaintenance() {
    safeRequestIdleCallback(async () => {
      if ($nucleumDatafnStatus.nucleumMode === "sync" && !isDebug) {
        await reconcileDatafnNow();
      }
      await refreshNucleumDatafnStatus();
      await syncAccountPaidPlanFromExternalProvider();
    });
  }

  async function onAppear() {
    try {
      await recovery.uploadPendingCloudData();
      await refreshTimeZone();
      const isCloudUser = $nucleumDatafnStatus.nucleumMode === "sync";
      if (isCloudUser && !dev_isDisableSyncOnAppear) {
        await pullForegroundDatafn();
      }
      if (isExtensionEnvironment() || isDebug) return;
      performAppUpdateCheck();
      await refreshNucleumDatafnStatus();
    } catch (e) {
      logger.error({ at: "onAppear", error: e });
    }
  }

  async function initializeDatabase(options?: {
    isOfflinabilityEnabled?: boolean;
  }) {
    try {
      const isLiteMode = $context.isSheet;
      logger.log({
        at: "UserBaseLayer.initializeData",
        isLiteMode,
        dataMode: $account.dataMode
      });
      if (!isLiteMode && !isDebug && !$context.isInOfflineMode) {
        await refreshAppStaticData();
      }
      const dapId = await getDapId();

      const hasUserSpace = Boolean($account.userId || $account.userInfo?.id);
      if ($account.dataMode !== UserDataMode.LOCAL && !hasUserSpace) {
        error = "User id not found. Please try again later.";
        return;
      }
      loadingMessage = loadingMessages.cloneDown;
      const runtime = await initializeNucleumDatafn({
        product: $appStore.product,
        account: $account,
        env: $appStore.env,
        appVersion: $appStore.version + "." + $appStore.build,
        dapId: dapId!,
        isOffline: $context.isInOfflineMode,
        isOfflinabilityEnabled: options?.isOfflinabilityEnabled
      });
      logger.log({
        at: "UserBaseLayer.initializeData - datafn",
        mode: runtime.mode,
        namespace: runtime.namespace,
        storageDbName: runtime.storageDbName,
        os: $context.os,
        isEmbed: $context.isEmbed,
        embed: $context.embed,
        userAgent: navigator.userAgent
      });
      return runtime;
    } catch (e) {
      error = "Unable to initialize local data. Please try again later.";
      logger.error({ at: "initializeDatabase", error: e });
    }
  }

  function handlePersistAppearance(event: any) {
    userPreferences.setAppearance(event.detail);
  }

  function handleAppLoadingStatus(event: any) {
    logger.log({ at: "handleAppLoadingStatus", event });
    const detail = event.detail;
    if (detail.message || detail.subMessage) {
      isAppLoading = true;
    }
    if (detail.isFinished) {
      setTimeout(() => {
        isAppLoading = false;
      }, 500);
    }
    if (detail.message !== undefined) {
      loadingMessage.message = detail.message;
    }
    if (detail.subMessage !== undefined) {
      loadingMessage.subMessage = detail.subMessage;
    }
    if (detail.duration !== undefined) {
      loadingMessage.duration = detail.duration;
    }
    if (detail.percentage !== undefined) {
      loadingMessage.percentage = detail.percentage;
    }
  }

  function handleAddToRecents(event: any) {
    logger.log({ at: "handleAddToRecents", event });
    const { record, type, timestamp } = event.detail;
    recentsStore.add(record, { type, timestamp });
  }

  async function handleMessageFromParent(event: MessageEvent) {
    try {
      const parsed = parseNativeMessage(event);
      if (!parsed) return;
      if (
        await handleNativePurchase(parsed, {
          verifying: () => {
            loadingMessage.message = "Verifying payment...";
          },
          finished: () => {
            isAppLoading = false;
          }
        })
      )
        return;
      if (handleNativeFileMessage(parsed)) return;
      if (parsed.type && parsed.id && parsed.data)
        embedBridge.setData(parsed.id, parsed.type, parsed.data);
    } catch (error) {
      logger.error({
        at: "handleMessageFromParent",
        error,
        eventType: event?.data?.type,
        origin: event?.origin
      });
    }
  }

  function addWindowEventListeners() {
    window.addEventListener(
      GlobalEvent.PERSIST_APPEARANCE_USER,
      handlePersistAppearance
    );
    window.addEventListener(
      GlobalEvent.APP_LOADING_STATUS,
      handleAppLoadingStatus
    );
    window.addEventListener(GlobalEvent.ADD_TO_RECENTS, handleAddToRecents);
    window.addEventListener("message", handleMessageFromParent);
    window.addEventListener("focus", onAppear);
    window.addEventListener("beforeunload", handleBeforeUnload);
    window.addEventListener("unload", handleBeforeUnload);
  }
  function removeWindowEventListeners() {
    window.removeEventListener(
      GlobalEvent.PERSIST_APPEARANCE_USER,
      handlePersistAppearance
    );
    window.removeEventListener(
      GlobalEvent.APP_LOADING_STATUS,
      handleAppLoadingStatus
    );
    window.removeEventListener(GlobalEvent.ADD_TO_RECENTS, handleAddToRecents);
    window.removeEventListener("message", handleMessageFromParent);
    window.removeEventListener("focus", onAppear);
    window.removeEventListener("beforeunload", handleBeforeUnload);
    window.removeEventListener("unload", handleBeforeUnload);
  }
  function handleBeforeUnload(event: any) {
    if (
      !isDebug &&
      ($context.isInOfflineMode || $account.dataMode === UserDataMode.LOCAL)
    ) {
      event.preventDefault();
      event.returnValue = "";
    }
  }
  onDestroy(() => {
    removeWindowEventListeners();
    subs.forEach((sub) => sub());
  });
</script>

1	# Application composition (@nucleum/application)
     2	
     3	Application wires independently owned implementations into a running product.
     4	It is not the default owner of connected components or workflows.
     5	
     6	## Permanent owners
     7	
     8	- composition: host registration, product presentation, product shortcut defaults, ordered assembly of owner-defined global and settings commands.
     9	- layers: startup ordering, account access gating, user layout assembly, modal orchestration and telemetry consent/lifecycle wiring.
    10	- chrome: product-connected snippets supplied to the independent shell, including native capture.
    11	- branding: product-identity adapters over portable visual assets.
    12	- paint: product-aware startup presentation and concrete action-component resolution.
    13	
    14	The root contains only this charter and the package manifest. New top-level
    15	owners require an explicit architecture decision and checker update.
    16	
    17	## Responsibilities owned elsewhere
    18	
    19	- shell/navigation and shell/layers: browser navigation, route decoding, platform classes and viewport handling.
    20	- shell/modal: modal chrome and dismissal; application layers choose the concrete content.
    21	- surfaces/library: mixed-resource rendering and bulk selection presentation; features/records owns record actions and bulk mutations.
    22	- surfaces/account: OAuth, session hydration, extension login and environment-change sign-out.
    23	- surfaces/subscription: plan reconciliation and native purchase outcomes.
    24	- surfaces/settings/data-recovery: recovery decisions and UI; persistence/migrations owns headless import mechanics.
    25	- surfaces/settings/about: application-update workflow.
    26	- surfaces/help: documentation, support, connected error recovery and shipped diagnostics.
    27	- surfaces/sharing: permissions and public-link workflows.
    28	- runtime: host detection, native message validation, service workers and log capture.
    29	- shared-state/app-context, preferences and files: application metadata, timezone preferences and native file responses.
    30	- ui/compositions: quick-access grids, hold-action presentation and point-map rendering.
    31	- features/memory/maps: memory popup content and its map adapter.
    32	
    33	Application keeps lifecycle sequencing and supplies narrow callbacks to the
    34	owning workflows. Do not move a large layer wholesale into another generic
    35	controller, service, state or utilities directory. Do not add compatibility
    36	re-exports at retired paths.
    37	
    38	## Verification
    39	
    40	Run npm run check:architecture, node tools/check/type-ownership.mjs, the product
    41	compiler checks and relevant unit suites. Compiler/import success does not
    42	prove browser, native purchase, legacy-data recovery or cloud behavior.
    43	
    44	For the presentation-host and settings splits, manually verify account sign-in,
    45	extension login, onboarding, branded loading, account navigation status,
    46	library search and empty states, backup and restore, E2EE controls, and cache
    47	actions on the Caddy HTTPS product hosts. Reopen settings and library surfaces
    48	after writes to confirm persistent results.

1	# `client/shell` — application shell: arrangement and navigation (`@nucleum/shell`)
     2	
     3	Charter: how the app is arranged and moved through, independent of what content
     4	fills it. Pure "where things go and how you move", never "what a screen does".
     5	
     6	## Owners
     7	
     8	`navigation` (URL/history, resource navigation), `topNav`, `bottomNav`,
     9	`leftPanel`, `rightPanel`, `trail`, `layers` (theme, metadata, embed),
    10	`overlays`, `modal`, `paint` (page and
    11	resource resolvers fed through the shared-state action renderer), `split views`,
    12	`tabs`, `sync` and `notifications` chrome.
    13	
    14	## Belongs here
    15	
    16	Anything that owns URL state, panel arrangement, tab/sidebar behavior, product
    17	menus, or shell events. If removing it would not change what any single screen
    18	does, only how screens are framed and reached, it belongs here.
    19	
    20	## Not here
    21	
    22	- Domain screens and workflows (account, library, settings, command) ->
    23	  `surfaces/`.
    24	- Portable domain-free UI -> `ui/`.
    25	- Content capabilities -> `features/`.
    26	- Sync scheduling -> `datafn/visibility-sync`; telemetry mechanics ->
    27	  `runtime/telemetry`; consent/lifecycle wiring -> application layers;
    28	  connected support -> `surfaces/help/support`.
    29	- Application composition layers that wire the running product together
    30	  (base/user layers, the action `ComponentResolver`, `AppLoadingView`, and the
    31	  settings action map) -> `application/`.
    32	
    33	## Dependency direction (enforced)
    34	
    35	Shell is acyclic: it must not import `application/`, `surfaces/`, or
    36	`products/`, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters through
    37	`@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome
    38	(brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status,
    39	capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props provided
    40	by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`).
    41	
    42	## Junk-drawer test
    43	
    44	A shell component may read navigation and shell state, but it must not contain a
    45	feature workflow. If it orchestrates a domain task (sign-in, billing, resource
    46	browsing), it is a surface, not shell.
     1	# `client/surfaces` — cross-feature product surfaces (`@nucleum/surfaces`)
     2	
     3	Charter: user-facing surfaces that are about the app itself or operate across
     4	all content features. Second-order UI: it composes `features/`, `shell/`, and
     5	shared state into product-level experiences.
     6	
     7	## Owners
     8	
     9	`account` (identity workflows), `subscription` (billing and native purchases), `onboarding`, `help` (docs, support, error recovery and shipped diagnostics),
    10	`settings` (including data recovery), `sharing`, `commandBar` + `commands` + `search` (command surface), `library`
    11	(resource browsing and rendering).
    12	
    13	## Why not `features/`
    14	
    15	Features are first-order content capabilities a user creates and manages
    16	(memory, focus, collections, spaces, calendar). Surfaces are about the product:
    17	identity, billing, settings, command dispatch, and browsing every resource type.
    18	
    19	## Import rules (enforced)
    20	
    21	- May import `features`, `shell`, `shared-state`, `runtime`, `datafn`, `ui`,
    22	  and `products`. Application-selected presentation enters through narrow
    23	  shared-state hosts configured before surfaces mount.
    24	- Must not import `application`; this would point a composed surface back at
    25	  its composition root.
    26	- `features/` must never import `surfaces/` — this edge is rejected by
    27	  `npm run check:architecture`.
    28	
    29	## Junk-drawer test
    30	
    31	- A first-order content capability? -> `features/`.
    32	- Pure arrangement/navigation chrome? -> `shell/`.
    33	- Product wiring (host-contract configuration, base layers)? -> `application`
    34	  composition.
    35	- Dev-only probes and experimental fixtures? -> `tools/`, stories, or delete.
    36	- Shipped troubleshooting actions and diagnostics? -> `help/diagnostics`, preserving their existing access gates.
     1	# `client/features` — user-facing content capabilities (`@nucleum/features`)
     2	
     3	Charter: the marquee things a user creates and manages. Each feature is a
     4	self-contained capability reached from outside only through declared entry
     5	points.
     6	
     7	## Owners
     8	
     9	`calendar`, `collections`, `focus`, `memory`, `records`, `spaces`, `system`.
    10	
    11	## Belongs here
    12	
    13	A cohesive content capability with its own UI, state, and logic.
    14	`records` owns connected record actions and bulk mutations; shared-state
    15	supplies their headless selection state and application-configured host.
    16	
    17	## Import rules (enforced)
    18	
    19	- May import `ui`, `shared-state`, `runtime`, `datafn`, and the application
    20	  **shell** surface only.
    21	- May **not** import `products` or application workflows outside the shell.
    22	- Cross-feature imports must target a path declared in
    23	  `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`; there is no barrel.
    24	
    25	## Junk-drawer test
    26	
    27	If the thing operates *across* features or is *about the app itself* — account
    28	and billing, the command palette, the resource library/browser, settings,
    29	onboarding, help — it is a **product surface** and belongs in the top-level
    30	`client/surfaces/` workspace (see `docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md`).
    31	`features/` must never import `surfaces/`; the checker rejects that edge.

    27	  `runtime/telemetry`; consent/lifecycle wiring -> application layers;
    28	  connected support -> `surfaces/help/support`.
    29	- Application composition layers that wire the running product together
    30	  (base/user layers, the action `ComponentResolver`, `AppLoadingView`, and the
    31	  settings action map) -> `application/`.
    32	
    33	## Dependency direction (enforced)
    34	
    35	Shell is acyclic: it must not import `application/`, `surfaces/`, or
    36	`products/`, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters through
    37	`@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome
    38	(brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status,
    39	capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props provided
    40	by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`).
    41	
    42	## Junk-drawer test
    43	
    44	A shell component may read navigation and shell state, but it must not contain a
    45	feature workflow. If it orchestrates a domain task (sign-in, billing, resource
    46	browsing), it is a surface, not shell.
     1	# `client/surfaces` — cross-feature product surfaces (`@nucleum/surfaces`)
     2	
     3	Charter: user-facing surfaces that are about the app itself or operate across
     4	all content features. Second-order UI: it composes `features/`, `shell/`, and
     5	shared state into product-level experiences.
     6	
     7	## Owners
     8	
     9	`account` (identity workflows), `subscription` (billing and native purchases), `onboarding`, `help` (docs, support, error recovery and shipped diagnostics),
    10	`settings` (including data recovery), `sharing`, `commandBar` + `commands` + `search` (command surface), `library`
    11	(resource browsing and rendering).
    12	
    13	## Why not `features/`
    14	
    15	Features are first-order content capabilities a user creates and manages
    16	(memory, focus, collections, spaces, calendar). Surfaces are about the product:
    17	identity, billing, settings, command dispatch, and browsing every resource type.
    18	
    19	## Import rules (enforced)
    20	
    21	- May import `features`, `shell`, `shared-state`, `runtime`, `datafn`, `ui`,
    22	  and `products`. Application-selected presentation enters through narrow
    23	  shared-state hosts configured before surfaces mount.
    24	- Must not import `application`; this would point a composed surface back at
    25	  its composition root.
    26	- `features/` must never import `surfaces/` — this edge is rejected by
    27	  `npm run check:architecture`.
    28	
    29	## Junk-drawer test
    30	
    31	- A first-order content capability? -> `features/`.
    32	- Pure arrangement/navigation chrome? -> `shell/`.
    33	- Product wiring (host-contract configuration, base layers)? -> `application`
    34	  composition.
    35	- Dev-only probes and experimental fixtures? -> `tools/`, stories, or delete.
    36	- Shipped troubleshooting actions and diagnostics? -> `help/diagnostics`, preserving their existing access gates.
     1	# `client/features` — user-facing content capabilities (`@nucleum/features`)
     2	
     3	Charter: the marquee things a user creates and manages. Each feature is a
     4	self-contained capability reached from outside only through declared entry
     5	points.
     6	
     7	## Owners
     8	
     9	`calendar`, `collections`, `focus`, `memory`, `records`, `spaces`, `system`.
    10	
    11	## Belongs here
    12	
    13	A cohesive content capability with its own UI, state, and logic.
    14	`records` owns connected record actions and bulk mutations; shared-state
    15	supplies their headless selection state and application-configured host.
    16	
    17	## Import rules (enforced)
    18	
    19	- May import `ui`, `shared-state`, `runtime`, `datafn`, and the application
    20	  **shell** surface only.
    21	- May **not** import `products` or application workflows outside the shell.
    22	- Cross-feature imports must target a path declared in
    23	  `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`; there is no barrel.
    24	
    25	## Junk-drawer test
    26	
    27	If the thing operates *across* features or is *about the app itself* — account
    28	and billing, the command palette, the resource library/browser, settings,
    29	onboarding, help — it is a **product surface** and belongs in the top-level
    30	`client/surfaces/` workspace (see `docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md`).
    31	`features/` must never import `surfaces/`; the checker rejects that edge.
"}}}

content.text:
`client/application` still has a purpose in the new design: it is the **composition root**. It starts the running app and connects code owned by the other packages. It should be small, and it should not become the home for anything merely used across the app. That is the distinction the refactor is aiming for in the [application charter](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/README.md:1).

| Owner | The question it answers | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| [Features](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/features/README.md:1) | What content can a user create and manage? | Memory, focus, collections, calendar, record actions. |
| [Surfaces](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/surfaces/README.md:1) | What app-level task or cross-feature screen is the user using? | Account, settings, subscription, search, command bar, library. |
| [Shell](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/shell/README.md:1) | Where does content appear, and how does the user navigate to it? | URL navigation, tabs, sidebars, panels, split views, modal chrome. |
| [Application](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/README.md:6) | How are those owners connected and started for this product? | Register hosts, assemble commands, mount startup layers, supply connected chrome. |

The dependency rule makes this concrete: features cannot reach into surfaces or application; shell cannot reach into surfaces, products, or application; application can connect them at the top. For example, a record action belongs to `features/records`, browsing records belongs to `surfaces/library`, its panel and URL behavior belong to `shell`, and registering the renderer that connects them belongs to `application`.

## What remains in `client/application`

There are **19 source files**, in five bounded areas:

| Area | Why it stays |
|---|---|
| [composition](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts:1) | Registers the concrete command, renderer, navigation, shortcut, file, product, and UI hosts. [global-commands.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/composition/global-commands.ts:1) assembles commands defined by their owners. This is the clearest composition-root work. |
| [layers](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/layers/BaseLayer.svelte:1) | `BaseLayer` and `UserBaseLayer` control startup order and mount the resulting app. [AuthGuard](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/layers/AuthGuard.svelte:1) applies the product’s access requirement while delegating session work to account. The telemetry layers connect consent to script mounting. |
| [chrome](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/chrome/WiredTopNav.svelte:1) | Supplies account, search, library, branding, offline, and capture content as snippets to shell components. This lets the shell remain independent of those implementations. |
| [branding](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/branding/SubAtomLogo.svelte:1) | Chooses a product logo using persisted product identity; the actual visual logos remain in portable UI. |
| [paint](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/paint/ComponentResolver.svelte:1) | Resolves the app’s registered action to a concrete component. [AppLoadingView](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/paint/AppLoadingView.svelte:1) combines product branding and runtime context for startup. |

## What I would still refine

The folder is no longer a general catch-all, but I would **not call every file inside it settled**:

1. **[settings-actions.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/composition/settings-actions.ts:25)** is the clearest remaining ownership mismatch. Application should assemble settings actions; this file also defines the labels, icons, modal options, and components for every settings section, including Pointron-specific entries. Those definitions should live with `surfaces/settings` and the relevant product; application should retain only the final ordered assembly.

2. **[UserLayout.svelte](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/layers/UserLayout.svelte:49)** contains substantial URL-derived state and sidebar, panel, trail, and split-view arrangement. Those mechanics fit shell. I would split out that framing into shell and leave an application wrapper to supply connected chrome and the command-mode surface. Moving the whole file would make shell depend on surfaces.

3. **[ModalLayer.svelte](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/layers/ModalLayer.svelte:159)** mixes application action resolution with mini-player positioning, toast placement, modal stacking, and confirmation chrome. The latter are shell concerns. A shell-owned overlay frame with application-supplied content would sharpen the boundary; application should still choose the concrete action component.

4. **[startup-commands.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/composition/startup-commands.ts:9)** contains a hidden “Test app loading” action and the Rhombus placeholder, which is used from the top nav. Neither is really startup orchestration. The test action should be reviewed for removal or development-only registration; Rhombus should have an explicit shell or product owner.

So the answer to “why keep `application`?” is **startup and final wiring**. The next cleanup is to take the remaining *definitions and framing* out of a few application files, while keeping their final assembly there. I made no edits for this review.

We appreciate your interest and understanding. ### License This project is licensed under the AGPL-3.0 license. See the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for details. ### Contact For any questions, security reporting or feedback, please contact us at [hello@21n.co](mailto:hello@21n.co). ❤️ We extend our deepest gratitude to all the [OSS libraries and tools](https://github.com/21nOrg/nucleus/network/dependencies) that made this project possible. ## Code organization Product bundles in `apps/` compose user-facing features from `client/features/`. `client/ui/` is the domain-free, portable `@21n/ui` package: `elements` owns atomic controls, `compositions` owns reusable compound UI such as charts, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, and time controls, `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, `branding` owns pure visual brand assets, and `environment` plus `hosts` provide package-wide integration contracts. Portable UI receives product behavior through props or narrow hosts and remains independent of application state, runtime infrastructure, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Product-independent Nucleum behavior shared across features or products lives in named subdirectories of `client/shared-state/` and is imported from `@nucleum/shared-state/*`, including command ports and application events; this package must not depend on application, feature, or product implementations. `schema/` owns cross-layer contracts, `client/datafn/` owns storage and sync, and `services/account/` owns the backend. # Type and contract ownership

Tracked in TIDY-478; coordinated with TIDY-477. Module moves preserve runtime enum values and persisted representations.

## Conventions

Definitions stay beside their implementation unless independent consumers need a neutral contract. Feature contracts belong to the feature and external callers use explicit public entries. Portable UI controls own their structural prop and style types: primitives belong to `client/ui/elements`, package-wide host contracts belong to `client/ui/hosts`, portable platform state belongs to `client/ui/environment`, domain-neutral composition contracts belong to `client/ui/compositions`, generic DOM-action contracts belong to `client/ui/actions`, and visual asset contracts belong with `client/ui/icons`, `client/ui/illustrations`, or `client/ui/branding`. Those contracts must not derive from schema records, DataFn resources, runtime types, application actions, or state interfaces; owning adapters translate domain models at the UI boundary. Keyboard contracts are shared by controls and application shortcuts. Application action contracts belong to client configuration; shared command-host and event contracts belong to `client/shared-state/commands` and `client/shared-state/events`; resource-panel and notification models belong to their named capabilities. Browser ambient declarations live in client/ambient.

Schema owns cross-layer account, subscription, and legacy persistence wire contracts. Shared account contracts must not import client modules. Legacy serialized formats remain distinct from current DataFn records: deriving them from a newer schema would change their accepted shape. Generated AuthFn and DataFn/Drizzle files remain owned by services/account generation scripts and are never manually rewritten. Type-only dependencies use import type; enums used at runtime retain value imports.

The global client/types and shared/types packages are retired, without replacement catch-all packages or compatibility exports. Splits use direct imports to the actual owner. Billing presentation fields remain in surfaces/subscription; wire enums and billing data belong to schema/account. Store interfaces are separated from legacy mutation/filter wire contracts. Markdown validation and responsive text truncation leave shared utilities for their frontend owners.

## Current ownership follow-up

Product menu contracts live in `client/shell/navigation/app-menu.type.ts`. The inventory retains original paths as baseline provenance and updates destinations for current ownership. Portable UI, including both former icon systems, illustrations, and pure branding assets, is consolidated in the `@21n/ui` workspace, and the old elements, components, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, layout, state, and stores workspace aliases are retired. Product-independent cross-capability state, command ports, events, and services use named owners under `client/shared-state`; runtime context, persistent UI preferences, migrations, shell state, and product-aware branding adapters are colocated with their semantic owners. Historical manifest and alias snapshots remain as evidence; `currentPackages` records the 30 current manifests. `@nucleum/client`, `@nucleum/shared-state`, and `@21n/ui` are registered private source workspaces and are not independently publishable builds.

The empty legacy and catch-all client utility workspaces have since been retired; `currentPackages` now records 30 manifests. The current checker validates 383 module dispositions and 198 unchanged runtime enums, plus the explicitly audited retirement of the disconnected shell cache's `CacheKey` enum. No other runtime-enum retirement is exempted.

The following migration checklist and audit evidence describe the TIDY-478 baseline. Current application, navigation, account, file, and command ownership is described in `client-boundaries.md`.

## Execution checklist

- [x] Inventory first-party declarations, imports, packages, aliases, and generated modules.
- [x] Define ownership and migration conventions before edits.
- [x] Complete module colocation and mixed-contract splits.
- [x] Retire global aliases/packages and update all callers.
- [x] Enforce contract ownership and audit schema derivation and exceptions.
- [x] Verify products, services, extensions, shared packages, and relevant workflows.
- [x] Deliver coherent commits and record issue completion.

The inventory records every discovered module, its declarations and consumers, original ownership, and disposition. Locally declared types in implementation modules remain colocated; generated schemas remain generated; explicit type modules are reviewed against their consumers.

## Audit evidence and retained contracts

[type-ownership-inventory.json](type-ownership-inventory.json) records all 383 baseline type modules (1,168 declarations), their consumers and explicit dispositions, all 41 package manifests including nested deployment packages, and 462 exported constants. The baseline is commit `32154c37`; destinations reflect this migration. Embedded types remain beside their implementation. Packages without type declarations were audited for exports and dependencies too. Source aliases are build-time paths; `@nucleum/client` is a private source workspace, not an independently publishable package.

- `schema/account` owns profile and subscription wire data. `EmailParts` has one definition. `IPlan` is an application presentation model. The Apple verification response now has one source in the payment provider.
- `schema/legacy` owns the existing Surreal mutation, query, sync, resource-action and store-data encodings. The store-data enum is shared with query generation; Svelte observable interfaces remain in DataFn. Legacy contracts are not derived from modern database rows because their date unions and projected fields differ.
- `schema/datafn.ts` derives resource names from `nucleumDatafnSchema`; `schema/features.ts` derives resource/relation inputs from `defineSchema`. The installed schema API does not provide a compatible generic record inference helper for legacy UI models. Generated account/AuthFn and DataFn files remain unchanged and are produced by `db:generate` and `datafn:generate`; no authoritative schema changed in this task.
- Client `Resource`, `MetaResource` and `Product` compose schema values with the existing Next overlay. This composition is intentional; backend callers import schema directly. Memory node models include editor projections and legacy serialized dates and remain capability-owned rather than copying generated service database types.
- Native transcription model identifiers (`tiny.en`) and worker model identifiers (`Xenova/whisper-tiny.en`) are different protocols. Both live in runtime/inference, in separate native and worker modules with their original enum values. ImportSource and StepType enums in product import adapters likewise describe different supported inputs. Position types in the PDF annotator and media grid represent different coordinate contracts.
- Keyboard and interaction-mode definitions belong to `client/ui/elements`; package-wide portable host contracts belong to `client/ui/hosts`; resource-panel actions belong to `client/capabilities/resources`. Generic error codes are schema-owned, while user-facing error presentation stays in `client/capabilities/notifications` and application composition. Markdown validation belongs to memory, and responsive truncation belongs to the text primitive; shared utilities no longer import client implementations.
- Existing shared utility tests import the relocated validation/truncation functions directly. Their assertions remain unchanged; moving test ownership can be considered separately. Architecture production-layer rules exclude tests, but retired aliases are forbidden in tests too.
- The legacy relay request contract now lives with its server endpoint in `server/common/relay/relay.type.ts` and imports only schema-owned resource and query contracts. Server-to-client imports have no exceptions.
- Existing frontend implementation cycles are not claimed to be removed. Type-only imports erase type dependencies; runtime composition and feature API reduction remain coordinated with TIDY-477. This issue enforces cross-layer contract ownership and deliberate feature entries, not complete acyclicity of the application.

## Import and export rules

Import interfaces and aliases with `import type` or named `type` specifiers. Runtime enum uses must remain value imports. Do not re-export a moved definition from its former location. Public feature entries are listed in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json` and must match the feature package exports. DataFn and schema expose their new contracts directly. Do not create a new generic types package.

`npm run check:architecture` checks static imports, exports, dynamic imports, import types, CommonJS requires and Vitest mock imports. It rejects production schema/shared/server/service imports into client code, rejects all server-to-client imports, and rejects the retired package aliases. Historical specs and append-only `.conduct` reports retain references to the old layout as historical evidence; active guidance and configuration use the new owners.

## Verification

`npm run check:apps` passes for Nucleum, Memotron, Pointron and Timear with zero errors (379, 302, 308 and 0 warnings respectively). Account-service typechecking passes. The repository unit suite passes 277 tests with 3 skips; Playwright discovers 549 tests in 55 files. Focus session and Markdown persistence browser probes pass on the local HTTPS Nucleum host.

The share extension production build passes. Its check now reports two pre-existing errors instead of 47: unsupported `aria-label` on the debug-log button component and an optional NodeType at the route boundary. The original commit reproduces both. Timear extension build cannot initialize because the installed Sharp native binary is missing. Account memory integration cannot initialize because installed zod-to-json-schema imports an unavailable zod/v3 export; the original commit reproduces this failure. The separate legacy server suite has identical original/current results: 27 failing suites, 2 passing suites, 9 failed tests, 35 passed and 9 skipped. These include removed legacy Flux imports, missing provider dependencies, real-service integration failures and existing assertions. They are not evidence of migration regressions or passing end-to-end coverage.

`node tools/check/type-ownership.mjs` checks all recorded destinations and compares 199 runtime enum declarations to the baseline. `npm run check:architecture`, `npm run check:no-fixed-test-waits`, `npm run check:no-legacy-runtime`, `npm run lint` and the Turbo build graph dry-run pass. Lint has no package lint scripts and runs the configured static build prerequisite; it is not a claim of repository-wide formatting or ESLint coverage. Existing source aliases remain build-time dependencies; they are not indiscriminately added as workspace dependencies, which would create Turbo cycles. Contract consumers use the schema dependency and the existing frontend package/alias model.

Reproduce the browser checks with `node apps/e2e-playwright/scripts/probe-review-session.mjs` and `node apps/e2e-playwright/scripts/probe-markdown-ownership.mjs` while the local product server is running. Neither requires existing user data; each runs in a fresh offline browser context. Full cross-product Playwright, live auth/sync, native app packaging and production deployment were not exercised.

## Historical overlay/resource ownership refinement

TIDY-477 originally moved reusable popup contracts to the then-current elements package, overlay state to the then-current stores workspace, active-resource/selection state to its resource group, and generic ResourceError to DataFn. The current destinations are `client/ui/elements/modal`, `client/application/shell/overlays`, `client/capabilities/resources`, and DataFn respectively. The default error message belongs to `client/capabilities/notifications`. The inventory destinations follow the current owners so baseline enum validation stays reproducible. See client-boundaries.md for the permanent overlay host contract and the remaining application-specific dependencies.

Tracked in TIDY-478; coordinated with TIDY-477. Module moves preserve runtime enum values and persisted representations.

## Conventions

Definitions stay beside their implementation unless independent consumers need a neutral contract. Feature contracts belong to the feature and external callers use explicit public entries. Portable UI controls own their structural prop and style types: primitives belong to `client/ui/elements`, package-wide host contracts belong to `client/ui/hosts`, portable platform state belongs to `client/ui/environment`, domain-neutral composition contracts belong to `client/ui/compositions`, generic DOM-action contracts belong to `client/ui/actions`, and visual asset contracts belong with `client/ui/icons`, `client/ui/illustrations`, or `client/ui/branding`. Those contracts must not derive from schema records, DataFn resources, runtime types, application actions, or state interfaces; owning adapters translate domain models at the UI boundary. Keyboard contracts are shared by controls and application shortcuts. Application action contracts belong to client configuration; shared command-host and event contracts belong to `client/shared-state/commands` and `client/shared-state/events`; resource-panel and notification models belong to their named capabilities. Browser ambient declarations live in client/ambient.

Schema owns cross-layer account, subscription, and legacy persistence wire contracts. Shared account contracts must not import client modules. Legacy serialized formats remain distinct from current DataFn records: deriving them from a newer schema would change their accepted shape. Generated AuthFn and DataFn/Drizzle files remain owned by services/account generation scripts and are never manually rewritten. Type-only dependencies use import type; enums used at runtime retain value imports.

The global client/types and shared/types packages are retired, without replacement catch-all packages or compatibility exports. Splits use direct imports to the actual owner. Billing presentation fields remain in surfaces/subscription; wire enums and billing data belong to schema/account. Store interfaces are separated from legacy mutation/filter wire contracts. Markdown validation and responsive text truncation leave shared utilities for their frontend owners.

## Current ownership follow-up

Product menu contracts live in `client/shell/navigation/app-menu.type.ts`. The inventory retains original paths as baseline provenance and updates destinations for current ownership. Portable UI, including both former icon systems, illustrations, and pure branding assets, is consolidated in the `@21n/ui` workspace, and the old elements, components, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, layout, state, and stores workspace aliases are retired. Product-independent cross-capability state, command ports, events, and services use named owners under `client/shared-state`; runtime context, persistent UI preferences, migrations, shell state, and product-aware branding adapters are colocated with their semantic owners. Historical manifest and alias snapshots remain as evidence; `currentPackages` records the 30 current manifests. `@nucleum/client`, `@nucleum/shared-state`, and `@21n/ui` are registered private source workspaces and are not independently publishable builds.

The empty legacy and catch-all client utility workspaces have since been retired; `currentPackages` now records 30 manifests. The current checker validates 383 module dispositions and 198 unchanged runtime enums, plus the explicitly audited retirement of the disconnected shell cache's `CacheKey` enum. No other runtime-enum retirement is exempted.

The following migration checklist and audit evidence describe the TIDY-478 baseline. Current application, navigation, account, file, and command ownership is described in `client-boundaries.md`.

## Execution checklist

- [x] Inventory first-party declarations, imports, packages, aliases, and generated modules.
- [x] Define ownership and migration conventions before edits.
- [x] Complete module colocation and mixed-contract splits.
- [x] Retire global aliases/packages and update all callers.
- [x] Enforce contract ownership and audit schema derivation and exceptions.
- [x] Verify products, services, extensions, shared packages, and relevant workflows.
- [x] Deliver coherent commits and record issue completion.

The inventory records every discovered module, its declarations and consumers, original ownership, and disposition. Locally declared types in implementation modules remain colocated; generated schemas remain generated; explicit type modules are reviewed against their consumers.

## Audit evidence and retained contracts

[type-ownership-inventory.json](type-ownership-inventory.json) records all 383 baseline type modules (1,168 declarations), their consumers and explicit dispositions, all 41 package manifests including nested deployment packages, and 462 exported constants. The baseline is commit `32154c37`; destinations reflect this migration. Embedded types remain beside their implementation. Packages without type declarations were audited for exports and dependencies too. Source aliases are build-time paths; `@nucleum/client` is a private source workspace, not an independently publishable package.

- `schema/account` owns profile and subscription wire data. `EmailParts` has one definition. `IPlan` is an application presentation model. The Apple verification response now has one source in the payment provider.
- `schema/legacy` owns the existing Surreal mutation, query, sync, resource-action and store-data encodings. The store-data enum is shared with query generation; Svelte observable interfaces remain in DataFn. Legacy contracts are not derived from modern database rows because their date unions and projected fields differ.

## Import and export rules

Import interfaces and aliases with `import type` or named `type` specifiers. Runtime enum uses must remain value imports. Do not re-export a moved definition from its former location. Public feature entries are listed in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json` and must match the feature package exports. DataFn and schema expose their new contracts directly. Do not create a new generic types package.

`npm run check:architecture` checks static imports, exports, dynamic imports, import types, CommonJS requires and Vitest mock imports. <script lang="ts">
  import { navigation } from "@nucleum/shell/navigation/navigation";

  import { afterNavigate } from "$app/navigation";
  import { page } from "$app/stores";
  import type { Page } from "@sveltejs/kit";
  import { GlobalEvent } from "@nucleum/shared-state/events/event.enum";
  import { appStore } from "@nucleum/shared-state/app-context/app.store";
  import context from "@nucleum/client/runtime/context.store";
  import type { IAction } from "@nucleum/client/config/action.type";
  import { onDestroy, onMount } from "svelte";
  import { requireActionRenderer } from "@nucleum/shared-state/resources/action-renderer";
  import { requireProductConfig } from "@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host";
  import view from "@21n/ui/environment/view.store";

  const ComponentResolver = requireActionRenderer();
  const productConfig = requireProductConfig();

  let {
    prefix = undefined,
    cmdPageLaunch = undefined
  }: {
    prefix?: string;
    cmdPageLaunch?: string;
  } = $props();

  let action = $state<IAction | null>(null);
  let pageSub: any;
  let pendingRefreshes = $state<number[]>([]);
  const fileBasedRoutes = ["cparchived"];
  function resolvePath(pageData?: Page) {
    if (cmdPageLaunch) {
      return cmdPageLaunch;
    }
    if ($context.isSheet) {
      return $appStore.sheetPath;
    }
    let currentPath =
      pageData?.url?.pathname ??
      (typeof window !== "undefined" ? window.location.pathname : "");
    currentPath = currentPath.replace(/^\/+|\/+$/g, "");
    if (prefix) {
      currentPath = prefix + "/" + currentPath;
    }
    return currentPath?.endsWith("/") ? currentPath.slice(0, -1) : currentPath;
  }

  function queueRefresh() {
    [0, 50, 200].forEach((delay) => {
      const timeoutId = window.setTimeout(() => {
        refresh();
        pendingRefreshes = pendingRefreshes.filter((id) => id !== timeoutId);
      }, delay);
      pendingRefreshes = [...pendingRefreshes, timeoutId];
    });
  }

  afterNavigate(() => {
    queueRefresh();
  });

  onMount(() => {
    const refreshFromWindow = () => {
      queueRefresh();
    };
    pageSub = page.subscribe(async (pageData) => {
      await refresh(pageData);
    });
    window.addEventListener("popstate", refreshFromWindow);
    window.addEventListener(GlobalEvent.CUSTOM_NAVIGATION, refreshFromWindow);
    queueRefresh();
    return () => {
      pageSub?.();
      window.removeEventListener("popstate", refreshFromWindow);
      window.removeEventListener(
        GlobalEvent.CUSTOM_NAVIGATION,
        refreshFromWindow
      );
      pendingRefreshes.forEach((id) => window.clearTimeout(id));
      pendingRefreshes = [];
    };
  });
  onDestroy(() => {
    pageSub?.();
  });
  async function refresh(pageData?: Page) {
    const path = resolvePath(pageData);
    if (
      fileBasedRoutes.some((x) => window.location.pathname.startsWith("/" + x))
    ) {
      return;
    }
    if (path === "" || path === "index.html") {
      const homePath = $view.isPortrait
        ? productConfig.homePathPt
        : productConfig.homePath;
      navigation.gotoPath(homePath);
      return;
    } else if (!path) {
      navigation.gotoPath("/404");
      return;
    }

    action = appStore.resolveComponentFromPath(path);

    if (!action) {
      if (path === "index.html") navigation.gotoPath("/");
      else navigation.gotoPath("/404", { queryParams: { path } });
      return;
    }
    $appStore.currentComponent = action;
    $appStore.isMenuHidden = action.isMenuHidden || $context.isSheet;
  }
</script>

{#if action}
  <ComponentResolver
    path={action.path ?? action.action}
    params={action.componentParams}
  />
{/if}
<script lang="ts">
  import { requireCommandHost } from "@nucleum/shared-state/commands/command-host";

  import { logger } from "@nucleum/client/runtime/logging/logger";
  import { Resource } from "@nucleum/datafn/resource.enum";
  import { AccessMode } from "@nucleum/datafn/resource.type";
  import {
    determineResourceType,
    isSameResource
  } from "@nucleum/datafn/resource.utils";
  import { appStore } from "@nucleum/shared-state/app-context/app.store";
  import { requireActionRenderer } from "@nucleum/shared-state/resources/action-renderer";
  import { onMount } from "svelte";

  const ComponentResolver = requireActionRenderer();
  let {
    id,
    isFromSplitView = false,
    componentParams = {},
    accessMode = AccessMode.INLINE
  }: {
    id: string;
    isFromSplitView?: boolean;
    componentParams?: any;
    accessMode?: AccessMode;
  } = $props();
  let refreshId = $state<number>(new Date().getTime());
  let resolvedId = $derived(typeof id === "string" ? id : "");

  $effect(() => {
    if (accessMode === AccessMode.TAB && resolvedId) {
      setCurrentComponent();
    }
  });

  onMount(() => {
    const reloadResourceHandler: EventListener = (event) => {
      onReloadResource(event as CustomEvent<{ id: string }>);
    };
    window.addEventListener("reloadResource", reloadResourceHandler);
    return () => {
      window.removeEventListener("reloadResource", reloadResourceHandler);
    };
  });

  function onReloadResource(e: CustomEvent) {
    const resource = e?.detail?.id;
    if (!resource) return;
    if (resolvedId && isSameResource(resource, resolvedId)) {
      refreshId = new Date().getTime();
    }
    if (
      accessMode === AccessMode.TAB &&
      resolvedId &&
      isSameResource(resource, resolvedId)
    ) {
      setCurrentComponent();
    }
  }

  function setCurrentComponent() {
    try {
      if (accessMode !== AccessMode.TAB || !resolvedId) return;
      const resource = determineResourceType(resolvedId);
      if (!resource || resource === Resource.unknown) return;
      const action = requireCommandHost().resolveAction(resource);
      if (!action) return;
      appStore.update((s) => ({ ...s, currentComponent: action }));
    } catch (e) {
      logger.error("ResourceResolver.setCurrentComponent - error", e);
    }
  }
</script>

{#if resolvedId}
  {#key refreshId + resolvedId}
    <ComponentResolver
      path={resolvedId.split(":")[0]}
      params={{
        id: resolvedId,
        isFromSplitView,
        accessMode,
        ...componentParams
      }}
    />
  {/key}
{/if}

Markdown editing and tags belong to memory; combinations belong to spaces. Product-independent shared client behavior lives in the `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace under explicit `app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`, `preferences`, `product`, `resources`, and `shortcuts` owners. Cross-layer billing contracts live in `schema/account`. 1. difference bw application/chrome and shell?
2. should we rename application/ to composition/ ?

1. difference bw application/chrome and shell?
2. should we rename application/ to composition/ ?

**`shell` owns the frame; `application/chrome` fills its connected slots.**

For example, [TopNav](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/shell/topNav/TopNav.svelte) owns the nav layout and behavior. [WiredTopNav](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/chrome/WiredTopNav.svelte) supplies the product logo, account picture, search input, and bulk edit bar. Those implementations belong to their own surface or product; application connects them to shell. This keeps shell from importing surfaces or products. If an `application/chrome` file grows into a workflow, that workflow should move to its owner and leave only the connection here.

**I would keep `client/application`, rather than rename it to `client/composition`.** Composition is its main job, but the package also owns startup layers, access gating, connected chrome, branding selection, and action rendering. It already has a `composition/` subfolder, so a top-level rename would either produce `composition/composition` or require another reorganization without improving ownership. The stronger safeguard is the current restricted set of subfolders and the architecture rule against new root workflows. See the [application charter](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/application/README.md:1).

content.text: application is the only catch-all like folder left and I want to rename it appropriately? what else can we rename if not composition?
application is the only catch-all like folder left and I want to rename it appropriately? what else can we rename if not composition?

I’d revise my earlier recommendation: **`client/composition` is the best name**. My objection was to a straight rename that would leave `composition/composition`, not to the name itself.

I’d rename the inner `composition/` folder to `wiring/`:

```text
client/composition/
  wiring/       # host registration and command assembly
  layers/       # startup and access gates
  chrome/       # connected shell adapters
  branding/     # product-aware logo selection
  paint/        # action and loading renderers
```

`client/app-host` is a reasonable second choice, but “host” already has a specific meaning in this codebase. `bootstrap` is too narrow for components used after startup; `app` and `integration` leave the catch-all concern intact.

A proper rename would also change `@nucleum/application`, all direct imports, docs, and architecture rules in the same refactor, with no old-path re-exports. I haven’t changed files in response to this naming question.

The current destinations are `client/ui/elements/modal`, `client/application/shell/overlays`, `client/capabilities/resources`, and DataFn respectively. The default error message belongs to `client/capabilities/notifications`. The inventory destinations follow the current owners so baseline enum validation stays reproducible. ./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:28:`client/ui` is the permanent domain-free `@21n/ui` package. `elements` owns atomic controls and UI-only types. `compositions` owns domain-neutral compound UI intended for present or future reuse, including charts, maps, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, file presentation, keyboard listeners, duration inputs, scroll containers, and time selectors. `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, and `branding` owns pure visual brand assets. Package-wide portable platform state belongs to `environment`, while dependency-inversion contracts shared across controls and compositions belong to `hosts`. A single current consumer does not make a composition feature-owned. `client/shell` (`@nucleum/shell`) owns the concrete product shell: navigation, panels, split views, tabs, trails, overlays, modal chrome, and the extension-support layers. `client/surfaces` (`@nucleum/surfaces`) owns cross-feature product surfaces: account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, the command surface (`commandBar`, `commands`, `search`), and `library` resource browsing. `client/application` retains the composition root (`composition/resource-hosts.ts`, `composition/shortcuts.config.ts`), the base/user application layers, shell overlay mounting, chrome integration adapters, and product-aware branding adapters. Markdown editing and tags belong to memory; combinations belong to spaces. Product-independent shared client behavior lives in the `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace under explicit `app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`, `preferences`, `product`, `resources`, and `shortcuts` owners. Cross-layer billing contracts live in `schema/account`. Keyboard and interaction-mode contracts live in `client/ui/elements/keyboard`; panel and error presentation contracts live in their capability owners. See [type ownership](type-ownership.md) for the complete inventory.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:36:- The application shell is acyclic: `client/shell` must not import application, surfaces, or products, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters only through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome (brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status, capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props wired by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`).
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:48:Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition. The application shell is the top-level `client/shell` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`), the only app-level layer features may consume. Cross-feature product surfaces live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`); surfaces may compose features, while features never import surfaces. The portable UI foundation is the single `client/ui` workspace, consumed through `@21n/ui/elements`, `@21n/ui/compositions`, `@21n/ui/actions`, `@21n/ui/icons`, `@21n/ui/illustrations`, `@21n/ui/branding`, `@21n/ui/environment`, and `@21n/ui/hosts`. Compositions may use the other UI layers, while elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts never depend on compositions. The entire package remains independent, directly and transitively, from application state, runtime infrastructure, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Domain-neutral compositions stay in UI when future shared use is intentional, even with one current consumer. Product-connected behavior enters through explicit props or narrow contracts under `client/ui/hosts`, configured from `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` or supplied by the owning shell or feature adapter. Shared state and utilities cannot transitively load application or feature composition at runtime. Explicit type-only edges are excluded from the shared-runtime reachability rule; cross-capability imports remain permitted through declared public entries, so the complete source graph is not claimed to be acyclic.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:59:Application and extension shells configure permanent overlay, resource-action, panel, shortcut, recents, record-renderer, action-renderer, portable action, shortcut, file, environment, logging, and haptic contracts in `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts`. Configuration runs from base, user, and extension shells before presentation or command execution. Shell and feature adapters provide view-specific props such as keyboard matching, time scales, and address resolution. Shared Markdown display owns portable parsing; memory owns Markdown editing. Portable file presentation, resource enums, event contracts, and action identifiers no longer depend on capability implementations.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:73:The connected offline-status indicator lives in `client/application/chrome`; shared elements and the shell do not read account session state. Application composition supplies the indicator to shell chrome.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:237:Portable illustrations live under `client/ui/illustrations`, and pure product/provider marks live under `client/ui/branding`. The product-aware `SubAtomLogo` adapter remains under `client/application/branding` because it reads product persistence and composes the portable marks. The portable external-logo renderer owns its provider identifiers and accepts integration configuration through props instead of importing account runtime state. The standalone `@21n/illustrations` and `@21n/branding` workspaces and aliases are retired.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:241:Cross-feature product surfaces (account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, command, search, and library) live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`). Surfaces may compose features, shell, shared state, runtime, and products; features must never import surfaces. This split dissolves the former catch-all role of `client/application`, which retains only composition, lifecycle orchestration, chrome/branding adapters, and startup/action rendering.
./README.md:61:Product bundles in `apps/` compose user-facing features from `client/features/`. `client/ui/` is the domain-free, portable `@21n/ui` package: `elements` owns atomic controls, `compositions` owns reusable compound UI such as charts, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, and time controls, `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, `branding` owns pure visual brand assets, and `environment` plus `hosts` provide package-wide integration contracts. Portable UI receives product behavior through props or narrow hosts and remains independent of application state, runtime infrastructure, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Product-independent Nucleum behavior shared across features or products lives in named subdirectories of `client/shared-state/` and is imported from `@nucleum/shared-state/*`, including command ports and application events; this package must not depend on application, feature, or product implementations. `schema/` owns cross-layer contracts, `client/datafn/` owns storage and sync, and `services/account/` owns the backend. Application composition lives in `client/application/`; account, settings, sharing, library and other workflows live in `client/surfaces/`; navigation, notification presentation and shortcut execution live in `client/shell`; UI-independent infrastructure lives in `client/runtime/`. State is colocated with app context, runtime, preferences, persistence, shell, or feature owners rather than a generic `client/state` directory.

./AGENTS.md:57:- The concrete shell, URL/history navigation, tabs, sidebars, overlays, and product chrome belong in the top-level `client/shell` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`).
