WARP.md:13:- `client/application/`: composition, lifecycle orchestration, chrome/branding adapters, and startup/action rendering.
WARP.md:27:App context does not implement navigation or command execution. Shared state exposes the command port; `client/surfaces/commands` executes commands whose definitions live with their semantic owners and whose ordered registry is assembled in application composition. The application shell changes URL/history and owns connected notification rendering plus global shortcut execution. Shortcut settings presentation belongs under `client/surfaces/settings/shortcuts`. Application and extension shells install command, overlay, resource, renderer, shortcut, recents, icon-asset, and UI-environment hosts through `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` before mounting consumers.
README.md:61:Product bundles in `apps/` compose user-facing features from `client/features/`. `client/ui/` is the domain-free, portable `@21n/ui` package: `elements` owns atomic controls, `compositions` owns reusable compound UI such as charts, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, and time controls, `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, `branding` owns pure visual brand assets, and `environment` plus `hosts` provide package-wide integration contracts. Portable UI receives product behavior through props or narrow hosts and remains independent of application state, runtime infrastructure, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Product-independent Nucleum behavior shared across features or products lives in named subdirectories of `client/shared-state/` and is imported from `@nucleum/shared-state/*`, including command ports and application events; this package must not depend on application, feature, or product implementations. `schema/` owns cross-layer contracts, `client/datafn/` owns storage and sync, and `services/account/` owns the backend. Application composition lives in `client/application/`; account, settings, sharing, library and other workflows live in `client/surfaces/`; navigation, notification presentation and shortcut execution live in `client/shell`; UI-independent infrastructure lives in `client/runtime/`. State is colocated with app context, runtime, preferences, persistence, shell, or feature owners rather than a generic `client/state` directory.
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:28:`client/ui` is the permanent domain-free `@21n/ui` package. `elements` owns atomic controls and UI-only types. `compositions` owns domain-neutral compound UI intended for present or future reuse, including charts, maps, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, file presentation, keyboard listeners, duration inputs, scroll containers, and time selectors. `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, and `branding` owns pure visual brand assets. Package-wide portable platform state belongs to `environment`, while dependency-inversion contracts shared across controls and compositions belong to `hosts`. A single current consumer does not make a composition feature-owned. `client/shell` (`@nucleum/shell`) owns the concrete product shell: navigation, panels, split views, tabs, trails, overlays, modal chrome, and the extension-support layers. `client/surfaces` (`@nucleum/surfaces`) owns cross-feature product surfaces: account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, the command surface (`commandBar`, `commands`, `search`), and `library` resource browsing. `client/application` retains the composition root (`composition/resource-hosts.ts`, `composition/shortcuts.config.ts`), the base/user application layers, shell overlay mounting, chrome integration adapters, and product-aware branding adapters. Markdown editing and tags belong to memory; combinations belong to spaces. Product-independent shared client behavior lives in the `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace under explicit `app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`, `preferences`, `product`, `resources`, and `shortcuts` owners. Cross-layer billing contracts live in `schema/account`. Keyboard and interaction-mode contracts live in `client/ui/elements/keyboard`; panel and error presentation contracts live in their capability owners. See [type ownership](type-ownership.md) for the complete inventory.
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:36:- The application shell is acyclic: `client/shell` must not import application, surfaces, or products, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters only through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome (brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status, capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props wired by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`).
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:48:Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition. The application shell is the top-level `client/shell` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`), the only app-level layer features may consume. Cross-feature product surfaces live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`); surfaces may compose features, while features never import surfaces. The portable UI foundation is the single `client/ui` workspace, consumed through `@21n/ui/elements`, `@21n/ui/compositions`, `@21n/ui/actions`, `@21n/ui/icons`, `@21n/ui/illustrations`, `@21n/ui/branding`, `@21n/ui/environment`, and `@21n/ui/hosts`. Compositions may use the other UI layers, while elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts never depend on compositions. The entire package remains independent, directly and transitively, from application state, runtime infrastructure, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Domain-neutral compositions stay in UI when future shared use is intentional, even with one current consumer. Product-connected behavior enters through explicit props or narrow contracts under `client/ui/hosts`, configured from `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` or supplied by the owning shell or feature adapter. Shared state and utilities cannot transitively load application or feature composition at runtime. Explicit type-only edges are excluded from the shared-runtime reachability rule; cross-capability imports remain permitted through declared public entries, so the complete source graph is not claimed to be acyclic.
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:59:Application and extension shells configure permanent overlay, resource-action, panel, shortcut, recents, record-renderer, action-renderer, portable action, shortcut, file, environment, logging, and haptic contracts in `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts`. Configuration runs from base, user, and extension shells before presentation or command execution. Shell and feature adapters provide view-specific props such as keyboard matching, time scales, and address resolution. Shared Markdown display owns portable parsing; memory owns Markdown editing. Portable file presentation, resource enums, event contracts, and action identifiers no longer depend on capability implementations.
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:73:The connected offline-status indicator lives in `client/application/chrome`; shared elements and the shell do not read account session state. Application composition supplies the indicator to shell chrome.
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:119:`application/composition/global-commands.ts` preserves their original ordering;
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:237:Portable illustrations live under `client/ui/illustrations`, and pure product/provider marks live under `client/ui/branding`. The product-aware `SubAtomLogo` adapter remains under `client/application/branding` because it reads product persistence and composes the portable marks. The portable external-logo renderer owns its provider identifiers and accepts integration configuration through props instead of importing account runtime state. The standalone `@21n/illustrations` and `@21n/branding` workspaces and aliases are retired.
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:241:Cross-feature product surfaces (account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, command, search, and library) live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`). Surfaces may compose features, shell, shared state, runtime, and products; features must never import surfaces. This split dissolves the former catch-all role of `client/application`, which retains only composition, lifecycle orchestration, chrome/branding adapters, and startup/action rendering.

./WARP.md:27:App context does not implement navigation or command execution. Shared state exposes the command port; `client/surfaces/commands` executes commands whose definitions live with their semantic owners and whose ordered registry is assembled in application composition. The application shell changes URL/history and owns connected notification rendering plus global shortcut execution. Shortcut settings presentation belongs under `client/surfaces/settings/shortcuts`. Application and extension shells install command, overlay, resource, renderer, shortcut, recents, icon-asset, and UI-environment hosts through `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` before mounting consumers.
./docs/architecture/type-ownership.md:65:TIDY-477 originally moved reusable popup contracts to the then-current elements package, overlay state to the then-current stores workspace, active-resource/selection state to its resource group, and generic ResourceError to DataFn. The current destinations are `client/ui/elements/modal`, `client/application/shell/overlays`, `client/capabilities/resources`, and DataFn respectively. The default error message belongs to `client/capabilities/notifications`. The inventory destinations follow the current owners so baseline enum validation stays reproducible. See client-boundaries.md for the permanent overlay host contract and the remaining application-specific dependencies.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:28:`client/ui` is the permanent domain-free `@21n/ui` package. `elements` owns atomic controls and UI-only types. `compositions` owns domain-neutral compound UI intended for present or future reuse, including charts, maps, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, file presentation, keyboard listeners, duration inputs, scroll containers, and time selectors. `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, and `branding` owns pure visual brand assets. Package-wide portable platform state belongs to `environment`, while dependency-inversion contracts shared across controls and compositions belong to `hosts`. A single current consumer does not make a composition feature-owned. `client/shell` (`@nucleum/shell`) owns the concrete product shell: navigation, panels, split views, tabs, trails, overlays, modal chrome, and the extension-support layers. `client/surfaces` (`@nucleum/surfaces`) owns cross-feature product surfaces: account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, the command surface (`commandBar`, `commands`, `search`), and `library` resource browsing. `client/application` retains the composition root (`composition/resource-hosts.ts`, `composition/shortcuts.config.ts`), the base/user application layers, shell overlay mounting, chrome integration adapters, and product-aware branding adapters. Markdown editing and tags belong to memory; combinations belong to spaces. Product-independent shared client behavior lives in the `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace under explicit `app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`, `preferences`, `product`, `resources`, and `shortcuts` owners. Cross-layer billing contracts live in `schema/account`. Keyboard and interaction-mode contracts live in `client/ui/elements/keyboard`; panel and error presentation contracts live in their capability owners. See [type ownership](type-ownership.md) for the complete inventory.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:36:- The application shell is acyclic: `client/shell` must not import application, surfaces, or products, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters only through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome (brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status, capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props wired by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`).
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:48:Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition. The application shell is the top-level `client/shell` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`), the only app-level layer features may consume. Cross-feature product surfaces live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`); surfaces may compose features, while features never import surfaces. The portable UI foundation is the single `client/ui` workspace, consumed through `@21n/ui/elements`, `@21n/ui/compositions`, `@21n/ui/actions`, `@21n/ui/icons`, `@21n/ui/illustrations`, `@21n/ui/branding`, `@21n/ui/environment`, and `@21n/ui/hosts`. Compositions may use the other UI layers, while elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts never depend on compositions. The entire package remains independent, directly and transitively, from application state, runtime infrastructure, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Domain-neutral compositions stay in UI when future shared use is intentional, even with one current consumer. Product-connected behavior enters through explicit props or narrow contracts under `client/ui/hosts`, configured from `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` or supplied by the owning shell or feature adapter. Shared state and utilities cannot transitively load application or feature composition at runtime. Explicit type-only edges are excluded from the shared-runtime reachability rule; cross-capability imports remain permitted through declared public entries, so the complete source graph is not claimed to be acyclic.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:59:Application and extension shells configure permanent overlay, resource-action, panel, shortcut, recents, record-renderer, action-renderer, portable action, shortcut, file, environment, logging, and haptic contracts in `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts`. Configuration runs from base, user, and extension shells before presentation or command execution. Shell and feature adapters provide view-specific props such as keyboard matching, time scales, and address resolution. Shared Markdown display owns portable parsing; memory owns Markdown editing. Portable file presentation, resource enums, event contracts, and action identifiers no longer depend on capability implementations.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:73:The connected offline-status indicator lives in `client/application/chrome`; shared elements and the shell do not read account session state. Application composition supplies the indicator to shell chrome.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:237:Portable illustrations live under `client/ui/illustrations`, and pure product/provider marks live under `client/ui/branding`. The product-aware `SubAtomLogo` adapter remains under `client/application/branding` because it reads product persistence and composes the portable marks. The portable external-logo renderer owns its provider identifiers and accepts integration configuration through props instead of importing account runtime state. The standalone `@21n/illustrations` and `@21n/branding` workspaces and aliases are retired.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:241:Cross-feature product surfaces (account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, command, search, and library) live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`). Surfaces may compose features, shell, shared state, runtime, and products; features must never import surfaces. This split dissolves the former catch-all role of `client/application`, which retains only composition, lifecycle orchestration, chrome/branding adapters, and startup/action rendering.
./docs/security/legacy-oauth-review.md:7:- `client/application/account/oauth.ts` constructs state from guest and host values. URL encoding is present, but the state is predictable and is not a one-time browser-bound nonce.

./README.md:61:Product bundles in `apps/` compose user-facing features from `client/features/`. `client/ui/` is the domain-free, portable `@21n/ui` package: `elements` owns atomic controls, `compositions` owns reusable compound UI such as charts, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, and time controls, `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, `branding` owns pure visual brand assets, and `environment` plus `hosts` provide package-wide integration contracts. Portable UI receives product behavior through props or narrow hosts and remains independent of application state, runtime infrastructure, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Product-independent Nucleum behavior shared across features or products lives in named subdirectories of `client/shared-state/` and is imported from `@nucleum/shared-state/*`, including command ports and application events; this package must not depend on application, feature, or product implementations. `schema/` owns cross-layer contracts, `client/datafn/` owns storage and sync, and `services/account/` owns the backend. Application composition lives in `client/application/`; account, settings, sharing, library and other workflows live in `client/surfaces/`; navigation, notification presentation and shortcut execution live in `client/shell`; UI-independent infrastructure lives in `client/runtime/`. State is colocated with app context, runtime, preferences, persistence, shell, or feature owners rather than a generic `client/state` directory.

./WARP.md:27:App context does not implement navigation or command execution. Shared state exposes the command port; `client/surfaces/commands` executes commands whose definitions live with their semantic owners and whose ordered registry is assembled in application composition. The application shell changes URL/history and owns connected notification rendering plus global shortcut execution. Shortcut settings presentation belongs under `client/surfaces/settings/shortcuts`. Application and extension shells install command, overlay, resource, renderer, shortcut, recents, icon-asset, and UI-environment hosts through `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` before mounting consumers.
./docs/architecture/type-ownership.md:65:TIDY-477 originally moved reusable popup contracts to the then-current elements package, overlay state to the then-current stores workspace, active-resource/selection state to its resource group, and generic ResourceError to DataFn. The current destinations are `client/ui/elements/modal`, `client/application/shell/overlays`, `client/capabilities/resources`, and DataFn respectively. The default error message belongs to `client/capabilities/notifications`. The inventory destinations follow the current owners so baseline enum validation stays reproducible. See client-boundaries.md for the permanent overlay host contract and the remaining application-specific dependencies.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:28:`client/ui` is the permanent domain-free `@21n/ui` package. `elements` owns atomic controls and UI-only types. `compositions` owns domain-neutral compound UI intended for present or future reuse, including charts, maps, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, file presentation, keyboard listeners, duration inputs, scroll containers, and time selectors. `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, and `branding` owns pure visual brand assets. Package-wide portable platform state belongs to `environment`, while dependency-inversion contracts shared across controls and compositions belong to `hosts`. A single current consumer does not make a composition feature-owned. `client/shell` (`@nucleum/shell`) owns the concrete product shell: navigation, panels, split views, tabs, trails, overlays, modal chrome, and the extension-support layers. `client/surfaces` (`@nucleum/surfaces`) owns cross-feature product surfaces: account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, the command surface (`commandBar`, `commands`, `search`), and `library` resource browsing. `client/application` retains the composition root (`composition/resource-hosts.ts`, `composition/shortcuts.config.ts`), the base/user application layers, shell overlay mounting, chrome integration adapters, and product-aware branding adapters. Markdown editing and tags belong to memory; combinations belong to spaces. Product-independent shared client behavior lives in the `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace under explicit `app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`, `preferences`, `product`, `resources`, and `shortcuts` owners. Cross-layer billing contracts live in `schema/account`. Keyboard and interaction-mode contracts live in `client/ui/elements/keyboard`; panel and error presentation contracts live in their capability owners. See [type ownership](type-ownership.md) for the complete inventory.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:36:- The application shell is acyclic: `client/shell` must not import application, surfaces, or products, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters only through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome (brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status, capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props wired by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`).
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:48:Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition. The application shell is the top-level `client/shell` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`), the only app-level layer features may consume. Cross-feature product surfaces live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`); surfaces may compose features, while features never import surfaces. The portable UI foundation is the single `client/ui` workspace, consumed through `@21n/ui/elements`, `@21n/ui/compositions`, `@21n/ui/actions`, `@21n/ui/icons`, `@21n/ui/illustrations`, `@21n/ui/branding`, `@21n/ui/environment`, and `@21n/ui/hosts`. Compositions may use the other UI layers, while elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts never depend on compositions. The entire package remains independent, directly and transitively, from application state, runtime infrastructure, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Domain-neutral compositions stay in UI when future shared use is intentional, even with one current consumer. Product-connected behavior enters through explicit props or narrow contracts under `client/ui/hosts`, configured from `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` or supplied by the owning shell or feature adapter. Shared state and utilities cannot transitively load application or feature composition at runtime. Explicit type-only edges are excluded from the shared-runtime reachability rule; cross-capability imports remain permitted through declared public entries, so the complete source graph is not claimed to be acyclic.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:59:Application and extension shells configure permanent overlay, resource-action, panel, shortcut, recents, record-renderer, action-renderer, portable action, shortcut, file, environment, logging, and haptic contracts in `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts`. Configuration runs from base, user, and extension shells before presentation or command execution. Shell and feature adapters provide view-specific props such as keyboard matching, time scales, and address resolution. Shared Markdown display owns portable parsing; memory owns Markdown editing. Portable file presentation, resource enums, event contracts, and action identifiers no longer depend on capability implementations.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:73:The connected offline-status indicator lives in `client/application/chrome`; shared elements and the shell do not read account session state. Application composition supplies the indicator to shell chrome.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:237:Portable illustrations live under `client/ui/illustrations`, and pure product/provider marks live under `client/ui/branding`. The product-aware `SubAtomLogo` adapter remains under `client/application/branding` because it reads product persistence and composes the portable marks. The portable external-logo renderer owns its provider identifiers and accepts integration configuration through props instead of importing account runtime state. The standalone `@21n/illustrations` and `@21n/branding` workspaces and aliases are retired.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:241:Cross-feature product surfaces (account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, command, search, and library) live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`). Surfaces may compose features, shell, shared state, runtime, and products; features must never import surfaces. This split dissolves the former catch-all role of `client/application`, which retains only composition, lifecycle orchestration, chrome/branding adapters, and startup/action rendering.
./docs/security/legacy-oauth-review.md:7:- `client/application/account/oauth.ts` constructs state from guest and host values. URL encoding is present, but the state is predictable and is not a one-time browser-bound nonce.

./README.md:61:Product bundles in `apps/` compose user-facing features from `client/features/`. `client/ui/` is the domain-free, portable `@21n/ui` package: `elements` owns atomic controls, `compositions` owns reusable compound UI such as charts, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, and time controls, `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, `branding` owns pure visual brand assets, and `environment` plus `hosts` provide package-wide integration contracts. Portable UI receives product behavior through props or narrow hosts and remains independent of application state, runtime infrastructure, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Product-independent Nucleum behavior shared across features or products lives in named subdirectories of `client/shared-state/` and is imported from `@nucleum/shared-state/*`, including command ports and application events; this package must not depend on application, feature, or product implementations. `schema/` owns cross-layer contracts, `client/datafn/` owns storage and sync, and `services/account/` owns the backend. Application composition lives in `client/application/`; account, settings, sharing, library and other workflows live in `client/surfaces/`; navigation, notification presentation and shortcut execution live in `client/shell`; UI-independent infrastructure lives in `client/runtime/`. State is colocated with app context, runtime, preferences, persistence, shell, or feature owners rather than a generic `client/state` directory.

./WARP.md:27:App context does not implement navigation or command execution. Shared state exposes the command port; `client/surfaces/commands` executes commands whose definitions live with their semantic owners and whose ordered registry is assembled in application composition. The application shell changes URL/history and owns connected notification rendering plus global shortcut execution. Shortcut settings presentation belongs under `client/surfaces/settings/shortcuts`. Application and extension shells install command, overlay, resource, renderer, shortcut, recents, icon-asset, and UI-environment hosts through `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` before mounting consumers.
./docs/architecture/type-ownership.md:65:TIDY-477 originally moved reusable popup contracts to the then-current elements package, overlay state to the then-current stores workspace, active-resource/selection state to its resource group, and generic ResourceError to DataFn. The current destinations are `client/ui/elements/modal`, `client/application/shell/overlays`, `client/capabilities/resources`, and DataFn respectively. The default error message belongs to `client/capabilities/notifications`. The inventory destinations follow the current owners so baseline enum validation stays reproducible. See client-boundaries.md for the permanent overlay host contract and the remaining application-specific dependencies.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:28:`client/ui` is the permanent domain-free `@21n/ui` package. `elements` owns atomic controls and UI-only types. `compositions` owns domain-neutral compound UI intended for present or future reuse, including charts, maps, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, file presentation, keyboard listeners, duration inputs, scroll containers, and time selectors. `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, and `branding` owns pure visual brand assets. Package-wide portable platform state belongs to `environment`, while dependency-inversion contracts shared across controls and compositions belong to `hosts`. A single current consumer does not make a composition feature-owned. `client/shell` (`@nucleum/shell`) owns the concrete product shell: navigation, panels, split views, tabs, trails, overlays, modal chrome, and the extension-support layers. `client/surfaces` (`@nucleum/surfaces`) owns cross-feature product surfaces: account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, the command surface (`commandBar`, `commands`, `search`), and `library` resource browsing. `client/application` retains the composition root (`composition/resource-hosts.ts`, `composition/shortcuts.config.ts`), the base/user application layers, shell overlay mounting, chrome integration adapters, and product-aware branding adapters. Markdown editing and tags belong to memory; combinations belong to spaces. Product-independent shared client behavior lives in the `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace under explicit `app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`, `preferences`, `product`, `resources`, and `shortcuts` owners. Cross-layer billing contracts live in `schema/account`. Keyboard and interaction-mode contracts live in `client/ui/elements/keyboard`; panel and error presentation contracts live in their capability owners. See [type ownership](type-ownership.md) for the complete inventory.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:36:- The application shell is acyclic: `client/shell` must not import application, surfaces, or products, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters only through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome (brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status, capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props wired by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`).
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:48:Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition. The application shell is the top-level `client/shell` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`), the only app-level layer features may consume. Cross-feature product surfaces live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`); surfaces may compose features, while features never import surfaces. The portable UI foundation is the single `client/ui` workspace, consumed through `@21n/ui/elements`, `@21n/ui/compositions`, `@21n/ui/actions`, `@21n/ui/icons`, `@21n/ui/illustrations`, `@21n/ui/branding`, `@21n/ui/environment`, and `@21n/ui/hosts`. Compositions may use the other UI layers, while elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts never depend on compositions. The entire package remains independent, directly and transitively, from application state, runtime infrastructure, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Domain-neutral compositions stay in UI when future shared use is intentional, even with one current consumer. Product-connected behavior enters through explicit props or narrow contracts under `client/ui/hosts`, configured from `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` or supplied by the owning shell or feature adapter. Shared state and utilities cannot transitively load application or feature composition at runtime. Explicit type-only edges are excluded from the shared-runtime reachability rule; cross-capability imports remain permitted through declared public entries, so the complete source graph is not claimed to be acyclic.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:59:Application and extension shells configure permanent overlay, resource-action, panel, shortcut, recents, record-renderer, action-renderer, portable action, shortcut, file, environment, logging, and haptic contracts in `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts`. Configuration runs from base, user, and extension shells before presentation or command execution. Shell and feature adapters provide view-specific props such as keyboard matching, time scales, and address resolution. Shared Markdown display owns portable parsing; memory owns Markdown editing. Portable file presentation, resource enums, event contracts, and action identifiers no longer depend on capability implementations.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:73:The connected offline-status indicator lives in `client/application/chrome`; shared elements and the shell do not read account session state. Application composition supplies the indicator to shell chrome.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:237:Portable illustrations live under `client/ui/illustrations`, and pure product/provider marks live under `client/ui/branding`. The product-aware `SubAtomLogo` adapter remains under `client/application/branding` because it reads product persistence and composes the portable marks. The portable external-logo renderer owns its provider identifiers and accepts integration configuration through props instead of importing account runtime state. The standalone `@21n/illustrations` and `@21n/branding` workspaces and aliases are retired.
./docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:241:Cross-feature product surfaces (account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, command, search, and library) live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`). Surfaces may compose features, shell, shared state, runtime, and products; features must never import surfaces. This split dissolves the former catch-all role of `client/application`, which retains only composition, lifecycle orchestration, chrome/branding adapters, and startup/action rendering.
./docs/security/legacy-oauth-review.md:7:- `client/application/account/oauth.ts` constructs state from guest and host values. URL encoding is present, but the state is predictable and is not a one-time browser-bound nonce.

WARP.md:27:App context does not implement navigation or command execution. Shared state exposes the command port; `client/surfaces/commands` executes commands whose definitions live with their semantic owners and whose ordered registry is assembled in application composition. The application shell changes URL/history and owns connected notification rendering plus global shortcut execution. Shortcut settings presentation belongs under `client/surfaces/settings/shortcuts`. Application and extension shells install command, overlay, resource, renderer, shortcut, recents, icon-asset, and UI-environment hosts through `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` before mounting consumers.
README.md:61:Product bundles in `apps/` compose user-facing features from `client/features/`. `client/ui/` is the domain-free, portable `@21n/ui` package: `elements` owns atomic controls, `compositions` owns reusable compound UI such as charts, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, and time controls, `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, `branding` owns pure visual brand assets, and `environment` plus `hosts` provide package-wide integration contracts. Portable UI receives product behavior through props or narrow hosts and remains independent of application state, runtime infrastructure, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Product-independent Nucleum behavior shared across features or products lives in named subdirectories of `client/shared-state/` and is imported from `@nucleum/shared-state/*`, including command ports and application events; this package must not depend on application, feature, or product implementations. `schema/` owns cross-layer contracts, `client/datafn/` owns storage and sync, and `services/account/` owns the backend. Application composition lives in `client/application/`; account, settings, sharing, library and other workflows live in `client/surfaces/`; navigation, notification presentation and shortcut execution live in `client/shell`; UI-independent infrastructure lives in `client/runtime/`. State is colocated with app context, runtime, preferences, persistence, shell, or feature owners rather than a generic `client/state` directory.
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:28:`client/ui` is the permanent domain-free `@21n/ui` package. `elements` owns atomic controls and UI-only types. `compositions` owns domain-neutral compound UI intended for present or future reuse, including charts, maps, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, file presentation, keyboard listeners, duration inputs, scroll containers, and time selectors. `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, and `branding` owns pure visual brand assets. Package-wide portable platform state belongs to `environment`, while dependency-inversion contracts shared across controls and compositions belong to `hosts`. A single current consumer does not make a composition feature-owned. `client/shell` (`@nucleum/shell`) owns the concrete product shell: navigation, panels, split views, tabs, trails, overlays, modal chrome, and the extension-support layers. `client/surfaces` (`@nucleum/surfaces`) owns cross-feature product surfaces: account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, the command surface (`commandBar`, `commands`, `search`), and `library` resource browsing. `client/application` retains the composition root (`composition/resource-hosts.ts`, `composition/shortcuts.config.ts`), the base/user application layers, shell overlay mounting, chrome integration adapters, and product-aware branding adapters. Markdown editing and tags belong to memory; combinations belong to spaces. Product-independent shared client behavior lives in the `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace under explicit `app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`, `preferences`, `product`, `resources`, and `shortcuts` owners. Cross-layer billing contracts live in `schema/account`. Keyboard and interaction-mode contracts live in `client/ui/elements/keyboard`; panel and error presentation contracts live in their capability owners. See [type ownership](type-ownership.md) for the complete inventory.
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:36:- The application shell is acyclic: `client/shell` must not import application, surfaces, or products, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters only through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome (brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status, capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props wired by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`).
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:48:Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition. The application shell is the top-level `client/shell` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`), the only app-level layer features may consume. Cross-feature product surfaces live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`); surfaces may compose features, while features never import surfaces. The portable UI foundation is the single `client/ui` workspace, consumed through `@21n/ui/elements`, `@21n/ui/compositions`, `@21n/ui/actions`, `@21n/ui/icons`, `@21n/ui/illustrations`, `@21n/ui/branding`, `@21n/ui/environment`, and `@21n/ui/hosts`. Compositions may use the other UI layers, while elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts never depend on compositions. The entire package remains independent, directly and transitively, from application state, runtime infrastructure, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Domain-neutral compositions stay in UI when future shared use is intentional, even with one current consumer. Product-connected behavior enters through explicit props or narrow contracts under `client/ui/hosts`, configured from `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` or supplied by the owning shell or feature adapter. Shared state and utilities cannot transitively load application or feature composition at runtime. Explicit type-only edges are excluded from the shared-runtime reachability rule; cross-capability imports remain permitted through declared public entries, so the complete source graph is not claimed to be acyclic.
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:59:Application and extension shells configure permanent overlay, resource-action, panel, shortcut, recents, record-renderer, action-renderer, portable action, shortcut, file, environment, logging, and haptic contracts in `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts`. Configuration runs from base, user, and extension shells before presentation or command execution. Shell and feature adapters provide view-specific props such as keyboard matching, time scales, and address resolution. Shared Markdown display owns portable parsing; memory owns Markdown editing. Portable file presentation, resource enums, event contracts, and action identifiers no longer depend on capability implementations.
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:73:The connected offline-status indicator lives in `client/application/chrome`; shared elements and the shell do not read account session state. Application composition supplies the indicator to shell chrome.
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:119:`application/composition/global-commands.ts` preserves their original ordering;
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:237:Portable illustrations live under `client/ui/illustrations`, and pure product/provider marks live under `client/ui/branding`. The product-aware `SubAtomLogo` adapter remains under `client/application/branding` because it reads product persistence and composes the portable marks. The portable external-logo renderer owns its provider identifiers and accepts integration configuration through props instead of importing account runtime state. The standalone `@21n/illustrations` and `@21n/branding` workspaces and aliases are retired.
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:241:Cross-feature product surfaces (account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, command, search, and library) live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`). Surfaces may compose features, shell, shared state, runtime, and products; features must never import surfaces. This split dissolves the former catch-all role of `client/application`, which retains only composition, lifecycle orchestration, chrome/branding adapters, and startup/action rendering.

# Client ownership and import boundaries

Tracked in [TIDY-477](https://linear.app/21n/issue/TIDY-477/enforce-architectural-boundaries-after-client-feature-and-datafn).

## Delivery checklist

- [x] Commit the existing reorganization separately from schema, session, and popover fixes.
- [x] Move shared focus preferences and sound state into focus ownership, retaining persistence keys.
- [x] Remove the composition/session-store cycle by passing fixed end times explicitly.
- [x] Move memory upload, search-result, and synced-id helpers out of product implementations.
- [x] Supply the graph layout from the product shell.
- [x] Move authentication, network authority, connectivity, and logging into non-UI runtime ownership.
- [x] Move the active-resource UI store out of DataFn and avatar/icon catalogs into UI ownership and initial app data into configuration.
- [x] Remove unused mutation-label helpers from DataFn and depend on the observable-store interface instead of its implementation.
- [x] Move shared product contracts and navigation metadata out of product implementations.
- [x] Enforce completed boundaries and declare existing public feature entry points.
- [x] Pass compiler checks for Nucleum, Pointron, Memotron, and account-service.
- [x] Pass seven schema tests, two focus-preferences tests, and three popover tests.
- [x] Pass four Nucleum focus browser scenarios with no page errors.
- [x] Update the approved existing-test import and mock paths.
- [x] Adapt the approved fixed-end-time test setup without changing expected durations; pass 127 tests across all 19 affected unit-test files.
- [x] Confirm Playwright discovers all 549 tests in 55 files after import updates.

## Ownership

`schema` owns resource definitions. `client/datafn` owns the client storage and sync runtime. `client/runtime` owns browser infrastructure such as account transport, network authority, connectivity, and diagnostic logging. `client/features` owns capability implementations. `client/products` composes those capabilities into product experiences. Client product identity composition lives in `client/config/product.type.ts`; cross-layer product identity lives in `schema/product.type.ts`; declarative navigation metadata lives in `client/config`.

`client/ui` is the permanent domain-free `@21n/ui` package. `elements` owns atomic controls and UI-only types. `compositions` owns domain-neutral compound UI intended for present or future reuse, including charts, maps, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, file presentation, keyboard listeners, duration inputs, scroll containers, and time selectors. `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, and `branding` owns pure visual brand assets. Package-wide portable platform state belongs to `environment`, while dependency-inversion contracts shared across controls and compositions belong to `hosts`. A single current consumer does not make a composition feature-owned. `client/shell` (`@nucleum/shell`) owns the concrete product shell: navigation, panels, split views, tabs, trails, overlays, modal chrome, and the extension-support layers. `client/surfaces` (`@nucleum/surfaces`) owns cross-feature product surfaces: account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, the command surface (`commandBar`, `commands`, `search`), and `library` resource browsing. `client/application` retains the composition root (`composition/resource-hosts.ts`, `composition/shortcuts.config.ts`), the base/user application layers, shell overlay mounting, chrome integration adapters, and product-aware branding adapters. Markdown editing and tags belong to memory; combinations belong to spaces. Product-independent shared client behavior lives in the `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace under explicit `app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`, `preferences`, `product`, `resources`, and `shortcuts` owners. Cross-layer billing contracts live in `schema/account`. Keyboard and interaction-mode contracts live in `client/ui/elements/keyboard`; panel and error presentation contracts live in their capability owners. See [type ownership](type-ownership.md) for the complete inventory.

## Enforced rules

Run `npm run check:architecture`. CI and the root lint command run the same check. It resolves relative imports, source aliases, dynamic imports, and TypeScript import types in TypeScript and Svelte scripts.

- Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition; the top-level shell is the only app-level layer features may consume. Surfaces may compose features; features must never import surfaces.
- Surfaces must not import application composition. Product presentation and action rendering enter surfaces through narrow shared-state hosts installed by application composition.
- The application shell is acyclic: `client/shell` must not import application, surfaces, or products, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters only through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome (brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status, capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props wired by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`).
- Portable UI cannot directly or transitively import application state, runtime, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, or domain state.
- Compositions may use elements, actions, environment, and hosts; those lower UI layers cannot import compositions.
- Shared state cannot directly or transitively import application, feature, or product implementations.
- DataFn and runtime files cannot directly import features, products, application composition or shell, portable UI, or shared client state and services.
- Composition calculations cannot import the session singleton.
- A caller outside a capability must use a source file explicitly listed in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`.

The feature entry-point list records the existing public surface, including individual components and type modules; it is not a barrel module. Additions require an explicit contract change. Package exports expose these same paths. Source aliases bypass package exports, which is why the source-level check remains necessary.

## Current architecture contract

Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition. The application shell is the top-level `client/shell` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`), the only app-level layer features may consume. Cross-feature product surfaces live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`); surfaces may compose features, while features never import surfaces. The portable UI foundation is the single `client/ui` workspace, consumed through `@21n/ui/elements`, `@21n/ui/compositions`, `@21n/ui/actions`, `@21n/ui/icons`, `@21n/ui/illustrations`, `@21n/ui/branding`, `@21n/ui/environment`, and `@21n/ui/hosts`. Compositions may use the other UI layers, while elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts never depend on compositions. The entire package remains independent, directly and transitively, from application state, runtime infrastructure, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Domain-neutral compositions stay in UI when future shared use is intentional, even with one current consumer. Product-connected behavior enters through explicit props or narrow contracts under `client/ui/hosts`, configured from `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` or supplied by the owning shell or feature adapter. Shared state and utilities cannot transitively load application or feature composition at runtime. Explicit type-only edges are excluded from the shared-runtime reachability rule; cross-capability imports remain permitted through declared public entries, so the complete source graph is not claimed to be acyclic.

`client/shared-state` is the single `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace. It groups product-independent Nucleum client behavior by semantic owner without turning `client/` into a list of service folders. Shared command ports and application events are shared state because they are consumed across features, products, extensions, and application composition; concrete command execution remains application-owned. Shared state may consume lower-level runtime, DataFn, persistence, schema, utilities, and portable UI contracts. They may not consume application workflows or shell implementations, user-facing feature implementations, or product composition, directly or transitively. Consumers import named subpaths such as `@nucleum/shared-state/preferences/preferences.store`; there is no root barrel, `shared`, `core`, generic `state`, or nested generic `stores` bucket.

Focus and memory event contracts live under `client/shared-state/events`; clipper
transport events live under `client/runtime/extensions`. App metadata belongs to
`client/shared-state/app-context`. Surfaces consume application-selected action
rendering and product visuals through named shared-state hosts.

Presentation ownership is separate from navigation ownership. Neutral breadcrumbs and scroll containers live in UI. `client/shell/navigation/components/AppBreadcrumbs.svelte` translates application resource and path metadata into structural breadcrumb items and callbacks. Sidebars, tabs, split views, panels, and trails remain in the application shell when they own URL state, resource resolution, product menus, shell events, or other application orchestration. A component moves to UI only when its public contract can be expressed without product or domain vocabulary.

Application and extension shells configure permanent overlay, resource-action, panel, shortcut, recents, record-renderer, action-renderer, portable action, shortcut, file, environment, logging, and haptic contracts in `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts`. Configuration runs from base, user, and extension shells before presentation or command execution. Shell and feature adapters provide view-specific props such as keyboard matching, time scales, and address resolution. Shared Markdown display owns portable parsing; memory owns Markdown editing. Portable file presentation, resource enums, event contracts, and action identifiers no longer depend on capability implementations.

The public feature API is enumerated in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`. Each has a static consumer outside its capability. The checker rejects unused public entries and private external imports. This reduces the previous 154 entries by moving shared contracts and infrastructure to their proper owners without introducing barrels or compatibility paths.

Registered workspaces declare their production source imports. `@nucleum/client` owns lower-level config and runtime; `@nucleum/shared-state` owns product-independent shared client behavior, application context, command ports, and events; `@nucleum/shell` owns the application shell; `@nucleum/surfaces` owns cross-feature product surfaces; `@21n/ui` owns all portable presentation and visual assets. Source workspaces bundled by an app declare co-hosted workspace requirements as peer dependencies; existing build dependencies remain dependencies. Peers describe the host's source compilation requirements without adding artificial Turbo build cycles. This is not a claim that each source package builds or installs independently. The checker verifies both resolved workspace and external package imports; test and story dependencies are outside this production-source check.

The narrow Library now mounts resource panes only after a resource is selected. A dedicated focus-capability test covers the portrait Library in Nucleum and Pointron; a seeded Recents probe verifies visibility before and after reload without page errors. Broader regression results are recorded below separately from the architecture checks.

## Application-state ownership follow-up

Product and application context lives in `client/shared-state/app-context/app.store.ts`. Tracked in [TIDY-477](https://linear.app/21n/issue/TIDY-477/enforce-architectural-boundaries-after-client-feature-and-datafn).

## Delivery checklist

- [x] Commit the existing reorganization separately from schema, session, and popover fixes.
- [x] Move shared focus preferences and sound state into focus ownership, retaining persistence keys.
- [x] Remove the composition/session-store cycle by passing fixed end times explicitly.
- [x] Move memory upload, search-result, and synced-id helpers out of product implementations.
- [x] Supply the graph layout from the product shell.
- [x] Move authentication, network authority, connectivity, and logging into non-UI runtime ownership.
- [x] Move the active-resource UI store out of DataFn and avatar/icon catalogs into UI ownership and initial app data into configuration.
- [x] Remove unused mutation-label helpers from DataFn and depend on the observable-store interface instead of its implementation.
- [x] Move shared product contracts and navigation metadata out of product implementations.
- [x] Enforce completed boundaries and declare existing public feature entry points.
- [x] Pass compiler checks for Nucleum, Pointron, Memotron, and account-service.
- [x] Pass seven schema tests, two focus-preferences tests, and three popover tests.
- [x] Pass four Nucleum focus browser scenarios with no page errors.
- [x] Update the approved existing-test import and mock paths.
- [x] Adapt the approved fixed-end-time test setup without changing expected durations; pass 127 tests across all 19 affected unit-test files.
- [x] Confirm Playwright discovers all 549 tests in 55 files after import updates.

## Ownership

`schema` owns resource definitions. `client/datafn` owns the client storage and sync runtime. `client/runtime` owns browser infrastructure such as account transport, network authority, connectivity, and diagnostic logging. `client/features` owns capability implementations. `client/products` composes those capabilities into product experiences. Client product identity composition lives in `client/config/product.type.ts`; cross-layer product identity lives in `schema/product.type.ts`; declarative navigation metadata lives in `client/config`.

`client/ui` is the permanent domain-free `@21n/ui` package. `elements` owns atomic controls and UI-only types. `compositions` owns domain-neutral compound UI intended for present or future reuse, including charts, maps, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, file presentation, keyboard listeners, duration inputs, scroll containers, and time selectors. `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, and `branding` owns pure visual brand assets. Package-wide portable platform state belongs to `environment`, while dependency-inversion contracts shared across controls and compositions belong to `hosts`. A single current consumer does not make a composition feature-owned. `client/shell` (`@nucleum/shell`) owns the concrete product shell: navigation, panels, split views, tabs, trails, overlays, modal chrome, and the extension-support layers. `client/surfaces` (`@nucleum/surfaces`) owns cross-feature product surfaces: account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, the command surface (`commandBar`, `commands`, `search`), and `library` resource browsing. `client/application` retains the composition root (`composition/resource-hosts.ts`, `composition/shortcuts.config.ts`), the base/user application layers, shell overlay mounting, chrome integration adapters, and product-aware branding adapters. Markdown editing and tags belong to memory; combinations belong to spaces. Product-independent shared client behavior lives in the `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace under explicit `app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`, `preferences`, `product`, `resources`, and `shortcuts` owners. Cross-layer billing contracts live in `schema/account`. Keyboard and interaction-mode contracts live in `client/ui/elements/keyboard`; panel and error presentation contracts live in their capability owners. See [type ownership](type-ownership.md) for the complete inventory.

## Enforced rules

Run `npm run check:architecture`. CI and the root lint command run the same check. It resolves relative imports, source aliases, dynamic imports, and TypeScript import types in TypeScript and Svelte scripts.

- Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition; the top-level shell is the only app-level layer features may consume. Surfaces may compose features; features must never import surfaces.
- Surfaces must not import application composition. Product presentation and action rendering enter surfaces through narrow shared-state hosts installed by application composition.
- The application shell is acyclic: `client/shell` must not import application, surfaces, or products, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters only through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome (brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status, capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props wired by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`).
- Portable UI cannot directly or transitively import application state, runtime, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, or domain state.
- Compositions may use elements, actions, environment, and hosts; those lower UI layers cannot import compositions.
- Shared state cannot directly or transitively import application, feature, or product implementations.
- DataFn and runtime files cannot directly import features, products, application composition or shell, portable UI, or shared client state and services.
- Composition calculations cannot import the session singleton.
- A caller outside a capability must use a source file explicitly listed in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`.

The feature entry-point list records the existing public surface, including individual components and type modules; it is not a barrel module. Additions require an explicit contract change. Package exports expose these same paths. Source aliases bypass package exports, which is why the source-level check remains necessary.

## Current architecture contract

Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition. The application shell is the top-level `client/shell` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`), the only app-level layer features may consume. Cross-feature product surfaces live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`); surfaces may compose features, while features never import surfaces. The portable UI foundation is the single `client/ui` workspace, consumed through `@21n/ui/elements`, `@21n/ui/compositions`, `@21n/ui/actions`, `@21n/ui/icons`, `@21n/ui/illustrations`, `@21n/ui/branding`, `@21n/ui/environment`, and `@21n/ui/hosts`. Compositions may use the other UI layers, while elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts never depend on compositions. The entire package remains independent, directly and transitively, from application state, runtime infrastructure, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Domain-neutral compositions stay in UI when future shared use is intentional, even with one current consumer. Product-connected behavior enters through explicit props or narrow contracts under `client/ui/hosts`, configured from `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` or supplied by the owning shell or feature adapter. Shared state and utilities cannot transitively load application or feature composition at runtime. Explicit type-only edges are excluded from the shared-runtime reachability rule; cross-capability imports remain permitted through declared public entries, so the complete source graph is not claimed to be acyclic.

`client/shared-state` is the single `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace. It groups product-independent Nucleum client behavior by semantic owner without turning `client/` into a list of service folders. Shared command ports and application events are shared state because they are consumed across features, products, extensions, and application composition; concrete command execution remains application-owned. Shared state may consume lower-level runtime, DataFn, persistence, schema, utilities, and portable UI contracts. They may not consume application workflows or shell implementations, user-facing feature implementations, or product composition, directly or transitively. Consumers import named subpaths such as `@nucleum/shared-state/preferences/preferences.store`; there is no root barrel, `shared`, `core`, generic `state`, or nested generic `stores` bucket.

Focus and memory event contracts live under `client/shared-state/events`; clipper
transport events live under `client/runtime/extensions`. App metadata belongs to
`client/shared-state/app-context`. Surfaces consume application-selected action
rendering and product visuals through named shared-state hosts.

Presentation ownership is separate from navigation ownership. Neutral breadcrumbs and scroll containers live in UI. `client/shell/navigation/components/AppBreadcrumbs.svelte` translates application resource and path metadata into structural breadcrumb items and callbacks. Sidebars, tabs, split views, panels, and trails remain in the application shell when they own URL state, resource resolution, product menus, shell events, or other application orchestration. A component moves to UI only when its public contract can be expressed without product or domain vocabulary.

Application and extension shells configure permanent overlay, resource-action, panel, shortcut, recents, record-renderer, action-renderer, portable action, shortcut, file, environment, logging, and haptic contracts in `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts`. Configuration runs from base, user, and extension shells before presentation or command execution. Shell and feature adapters provide view-specific props such as keyboard matching, time scales, and address resolution. Shared Markdown display owns portable parsing; memory owns Markdown editing. Portable file presentation, resource enums, event contracts, and action identifiers no longer depend on capability implementations.

The public feature API is enumerated in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`. Each has a static consumer outside its capability. The checker rejects unused public entries and private external imports. This reduces the previous 154 entries by moving shared contracts and infrastructure to their proper owners without introducing barrels or compatibility paths.

Registered workspaces declare their production source imports. `@nucleum/client` owns lower-level config and runtime; `@nucleum/shared-state` owns product-independent shared client behavior, application context, command ports, and events; `@nucleum/shell` owns the application shell; `@nucleum/surfaces` owns cross-feature product surfaces; `@21n/ui` owns all portable presentation and visual assets. Source workspaces bundled by an app declare co-hosted workspace requirements as peer dependencies; existing build dependencies remain dependencies. Peers describe the host's source compilation requirements without adding artificial Turbo build cycles. This is not a claim that each source package builds or installs independently. The checker verifies both resolved workspace and external package imports; test and story dependencies are outside this production-source check.

The narrow Library now mounts resource panes only after a resource is selected. A dedicated focus-capability test covers the portrait Library in Nucleum and Pointron; a seeded Recents probe verifies visibility before and after reload without page errors. Broader regression results are recorded below separately from the architecture checks.

## Application-state ownership follow-up

Product and application context lives in `client/shared-state/app-context/app.store.ts`. Browser/embed environment context lives in `client/runtime/context.store.ts`; persistent UI preference state lives in `client/shared-state/preferences/ui-state`; legacy product-key migration belongs to `client/persistence/migrations`. URL/history and resource navigation live in `client/shell/navigation/navigation.ts`. Product command lookup/execution lives in `client/surfaces/commands/action-runner.ts`; the permanent shared `CommandHost` contract lives in `client/shared-state/commands/command-host.ts` and is installed from `resource-hosts.ts`. Application-wide events live in `client/shared-state/events`. No old methods delegate to the new owners.

Reactive account session state lives with the account runtime in `client/runtime/account/account.store.ts`. Authentication persistence, bootstrap, sign-in, sign-out, navigation, and DataFn teardown are coordinated by `client/surfaces/account/account-session.ts`. Deletion confirmation and cleanup orchestration live in `client/surfaces/account/account-deletion.ts`; subscription operations live in `client/surfaces/subscription/subscription.ts`; file conversion, thumbnail generation, signing, and local/remote storage live in `client/shared-state/files/file-upload.ts`. OAuth initiation and callback presentation belong to surfaces/account; legacy code exchange belongs to runtime/account.

The connected offline-status indicator lives in `client/application/chrome`; shared elements and the shell do not read account session state. Application composition supplies the indicator to shell chrome.

Product menu persistence lives beside navigation. Tab and sidebar mutations live beside the application shell; generic UI-state persistence belongs to the preferences capability. Shortcut persistence, matching, hints, and the host contract live in `client/shared-state/shortcuts`; global shortcut execution lives in `client/shell/shortcuts`, and shortcut settings presentation lives in `client/surfaces/settings/shortcuts`. Headless notification state lives in `client/shared-state/notifications`, while connected notification rendering lives in `client/shell/notifications`. Focus owns its scheduled notification queue, and the existing native transport delivers messages. Memory owns its word-count and PDF-overlay DOM actions. The unused Markdown action and empty `@nucleum/cx` workspace are retired, including active aliases and workspace declarations.

The former `client/stores`, `client/state`, `client/commands`, and `client/events` directories are retired. App context, appearance, commands, events, files, notifications, preferences, resources, and shortcuts have explicit owners under `client/shared-state`. Runtime environment state belongs to runtime, migration state belongs to persistence, the observable-store implementation belongs to DataFn, and overlay state belongs to the application shell. New state follows semantic ownership and must not recreate a catch-all `stores`, `state`, `shared`, or `core` directory; `client/shared-state` is the single approved shared-state workspace and keeps named owners with no root barrel.

Connected record menus and bulk mutations live in `client/features/records`; shared-state/resources retains selection state and the resource action host contract. DataFn resource selection, storage lifecycle, runtime policy and remote transport have named modules; `datafn.store.ts` owns the live client and lifecycle. Persistence separates client storage, device identity, legacy local storage, and the named legacy-backup operations. URL validation and product host parsing have named cross-layer utilities; memory owns its embed sanitizer, and the legacy Surreal query builder lives with server sync.

## Application composition refinement

### Utility workspace retirement (2026-09-22)

`client/utils` and `@21n/utils` are retired, including their workspace and aliases.

4. On native hosts, verify capture/haptics, purchase success/failure/restore,
   file delivery and the visible loading/onboarding outcomes.

## UI asset and shell consolidation

Portable legacy SVG/Rive icons, generated icon mappings, sprite resolution, and spinner components live under `client/ui/icons` and are imported through `@21n/ui/icons/*`. The UI package never imports the product static package; the application supplies asset URL resolution through the UI environment contract. The standalone `@21n/icons` and `@21n/icons-v2` workspaces are retired.

Portable illustrations live under `client/ui/illustrations`, and pure product/provider marks live under `client/ui/branding`. The product-aware `SubAtomLogo` adapter remains under `client/composition/SubAtomLogo.svelte` because it reads product persistence and composes the portable marks. The portable external-logo renderer owns its provider identifiers and accepts integration configuration through props instead of importing account runtime state. The standalone `@21n/illustrations` and `@21n/branding` workspaces and aliases are retired.

The concrete layout package is the top-level `client/shell` workspace. All callers use `@nucleum/shell/*`; the `@21n/layout` package, alias, workspace, and compatibility paths are retired. Features may use the shell's explicit navigation, overlay, and shell-presentation surface when participating in application composition, while imports from surfaces or application composition remain forbidden.

Cross-feature product surfaces (account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, command, search, and library) live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`). Surfaces may compose features, shell, shared state, runtime, and products; features must never import surfaces. This split dissolves the former catch-all role of `client/application`, now confined to `client/composition`, with explicit root files, `layers/`, and `chrome/`.

### Consolidation verification (2026-09-19)

- Architecture enforcement resolves 2,067 source files and 10,946 imports with zero violations; type ownership validates 383 dispositions and 199 unchanged runtime enums.

-Agents MUST reuse existing primitives, stores, and utilities when delivering changes. Prefer components in `client/elements/`, helpers such as `generateResourceId` and `generateSimpleRandomId`, and shared logic in `client/stores` or `shared/utils` instead of duplicating behavior. +

Remote synchronization MUST align with the account-service DataFn routes, schemas, generated Drizzle mappings, and lookup helpers under `services/account/src/datafn`, `services/account/src/db`, and `services/account/src/lookup`.
