# Type and contract ownership

Tracked in TIDY-478; coordinated with TIDY-477. Module moves preserve runtime enum values and persisted representations.

## Conventions

Definitions stay beside their implementation unless independent consumers need a neutral contract. Feature contracts belong to the feature and external callers use explicit public entries. Portable UI controls own their structural prop and style types: primitives belong to `client/ui/elements`, package-wide host contracts belong to `client/ui/hosts`, portable platform state belongs to `client/ui/environment`, domain-neutral composition contracts belong to `client/ui/compositions`, generic DOM-action contracts belong to `client/ui/actions`, and visual asset contracts belong with `client/ui/icons`, `client/ui/illustrations`, or `client/ui/branding`. Those contracts must not derive from schema records, DataFn resources, runtime types, application actions, or state interfaces; owning adapters translate domain models at the UI boundary. Keyboard contracts are shared by controls and application shortcuts. Application action contracts belong to client configuration; shared command-host and event contracts belong to `client/shared-state/commands` and `client/shared-state/events`; resource-panel and notification models belong to their named capabilities. Browser ambient declarations live in client/ambient.

Schema owns cross-layer account, subscription, and legacy persistence wire contracts. Shared account contracts must not import client modules. Legacy serialized formats remain distinct from current DataFn records: deriving them from a newer schema would change their accepted shape. Generated AuthFn and DataFn/Drizzle files remain owned by services/account generation scripts and are never manually rewritten. Type-only dependencies use import type; enums used at runtime retain value imports.

The global client/types and shared/types packages are retired, without replacement catch-all packages or compatibility exports. Splits use direct imports to the actual owner. Billing presentation fields remain in surfaces/subscription; wire enums and billing data belong to schema/account. Store interfaces are separated from legacy mutation/filter wire contracts. Markdown validation and responsive text truncation leave shared utilities for their frontend owners.

## Current ownership follow-up

Product menu contracts live in `client/shell/navigation/app-menu.type.ts`. The inventory retains original paths as baseline provenance and updates destinations for current ownership. Portable UI, including both former icon systems, illustrations, and pure branding assets, is consolidated in the `@21n/ui` workspace, and the old elements, components, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, layout, state, and stores workspace aliases are retired. Product-independent cross-capability state, command ports, events, and services use named owners under `client/shared-state`; runtime context, persistent UI preferences, migrations, shell state, and product-aware branding adapters are colocated with their semantic owners. Historical manifest and alias snapshots remain as evidence; `currentPackages` records the 30 current manifests. `@nucleum/client`, `@nucleum/shared-state`, and `@21n/ui` are registered private source workspaces and are not independently publishable builds.

The empty legacy and catch-all client utility workspaces have since been retired; `currentPackages` now records 30 manifests. The current checker validates 383 module dispositions and 198 unchanged runtime enums, plus the explicitly audited retirement of the disconnected shell cache's `CacheKey` enum. No other runtime-enum retirement is exempted.

The following migration checklist and audit evidence describe the TIDY-478 baseline. Current application, navigation, account, file, and command ownership is described in `client-boundaries.md`.

## Execution checklist

- [x] Inventory first-party declarations, imports, packages, aliases, and generated modules.
- [x] Define ownership and migration conventions before edits.
- [x] Complete module colocation and mixed-contract splits.
- [x] Retire global aliases/packages and update all callers.
- [x] Enforce contract ownership and audit schema derivation and exceptions.
- [x] Verify products, services, extensions, shared packages, and relevant workflows.
- [x] Deliver coherent commits and record issue completion.

The inventory records every discovered module, its declarations and consumers, original ownership, and disposition. Locally declared types in implementation modules remain colocated; generated schemas remain generated; explicit type modules are reviewed against their consumers.

## Audit evidence and retained contracts

[type-ownership-inventory.json](type-ownership-inventory.json) records all 383 baseline type modules (1,168 declarations), their consumers and explicit dispositions, all 41 package manifests including nested deployment packages, and 462 exported constants. The baseline is commit `32154c37`; destinations reflect this migration. Embedded types remain beside their implementation. Packages without type declarations were audited for exports and dependencies too. Source aliases are build-time paths; `@nucleum/client` is a private source workspace, not an independently publishable package.

- `schema/account` owns profile and subscription wire data. `EmailParts` has one definition. `IPlan` is an application presentation model. The Apple verification response now has one source in the payment provider.
- `schema/legacy` owns the existing Surreal mutation, query, sync, resource-action and store-data encodings. The store-data enum is shared with query generation; Svelte observable interfaces remain in DataFn. Legacy contracts are not derived from modern database rows because their date unions and projected fields differ.
- `schema/datafn.ts` derives resource names from `nucleumDatafnSchema`; `schema/features.ts` derives resource/relation inputs from `defineSchema`. The installed schema API does not provide a compatible generic record inference helper for legacy UI models. Generated account/AuthFn and DataFn files remain unchanged and are produced by `db:generate` and `datafn:generate`; no authoritative schema changed in this task.
- Client `Resource`, `MetaResource` and `Product` compose schema values with the existing Next overlay. This composition is intentional; backend callers import schema directly. Memory node models include editor projections and legacy serialized dates and remain capability-owned rather than copying generated service database types.
- Native transcription model identifiers (`tiny.en`) and worker model identifiers (`Xenova/whisper-tiny.en`) are different protocols. Both live in runtime/inference, in separate native and worker modules with their original enum values. ImportSource and StepType enums in product import adapters likewise describe different supported inputs. Position types in the PDF annotator and media grid represent different coordinate contracts.
- Keyboard and interaction-mode definitions belong to `client/ui/elements`; package-wide portable host contracts belong to `client/ui/hosts`; resource-panel actions belong to `client/capabilities/resources`. Generic error codes are schema-owned, while user-facing error presentation stays in `client/capabilities/notifications` and application composition. Markdown validation belongs to memory, and responsive truncation belongs to the text primitive; shared utilities no longer import client implementations.
- Existing shared utility tests import the relocated validation/truncation functions directly. Their assertions remain unchanged; moving test ownership can be considered separately. Architecture production-layer rules exclude tests, but retired aliases are forbidden in tests too.
- The legacy relay request contract now lives with its server endpoint in `server/common/relay/relay.type.ts` and imports only schema-owned resource and query contracts. Server-to-client imports have no exceptions.
- Existing frontend implementation cycles are not claimed to be removed. Type-only imports erase type dependencies; runtime composition and feature API reduction remain coordinated with TIDY-477. This issue enforces cross-layer contract ownership and deliberate feature entries, not complete acyclicity of the application.

## Import and export rules

Import interfaces and aliases with `import type` or named `type` specifiers. Runtime enum uses must remain value imports. Do not re-export a moved definition from its former location. Public feature entries are listed in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json` and must match the feature package exports. DataFn and schema expose their new contracts directly. Do not create a new generic types package.

`npm run check:architecture` checks static imports, exports, dynamic imports, import types, CommonJS requires and Vitest mock imports. It rejects production schema/shared/server/service imports into client code, rejects all server-to-client imports, and rejects the retired package aliases. Historical specs and append-only `.conduct` reports retain references to the old layout as historical evidence; active guidance and configuration use the new owners.

## Verification

`npm run check:apps` passes for Nucleum, Memotron, Pointron and Timear with zero errors (379, 302, 308 and 0 warnings respectively). Account-service typechecking passes. The repository unit suite passes 277 tests with 3 skips; Playwright discovers 549 tests in 55 files. Focus session and Markdown persistence browser probes pass on the local HTTPS Nucleum host.

The share extension production build passes. Its check now reports two pre-existing errors instead of 47: unsupported `aria-label` on the debug-log button component and an optional NodeType at the route boundary. The original commit reproduces both. Timear extension build cannot initialize because the installed Sharp native binary is missing. Account memory integration cannot initialize because installed zod-to-json-schema imports an unavailable zod/v3 export; the original commit reproduces this failure. The separate legacy server suite has identical original/current results: 27 failing suites, 2 passing suites, 9 failed tests, 35 passed and 9 skipped. These include removed legacy Flux imports, missing provider dependencies, real-service integration failures and existing assertions. They are not evidence of migration regressions or passing end-to-end coverage.

`node tools/check/type-ownership.mjs` checks all recorded destinations and compares 199 runtime enum declarations to the baseline. `npm run check:architecture`, `npm run check:no-fixed-test-waits`, `npm run check:no-legacy-runtime`, `npm run lint` and the Turbo build graph dry-run pass. Lint has no package lint scripts and runs the configured static build prerequisite; it is not a claim of repository-wide formatting or ESLint coverage. Existing source aliases remain build-time dependencies; they are not indiscriminately added as workspace dependencies, which would create Turbo cycles. Contract consumers use the schema dependency and the existing frontend package/alias model.

Reproduce the browser checks with `node apps/e2e-playwright/scripts/probe-review-session.mjs` and `node apps/e2e-playwright/scripts/probe-markdown-ownership.mjs` while the local product server is running. Neither requires existing user data; each runs in a fresh offline browser context. Full cross-product Playwright, live auth/sync, native app packaging and production deployment were not exercised.

## Historical overlay/resource ownership refinement

TIDY-477 originally moved reusable popup contracts to the then-current elements package, overlay state to the then-current stores workspace, active-resource/selection state to its resource group, and generic ResourceError to DataFn. The current destinations are `client/ui/elements/modal`, `client/application/shell/overlays`, `client/capabilities/resources`, and DataFn respectively. The default error message belongs to `client/capabilities/notifications`. The inventory destinations follow the current owners so baseline enum validation stays reproducible. See client-boundaries.md for the permanent overlay host contract and the remaining application-specific dependencies.

Tracked in TIDY-478; coordinated with TIDY-477. Module moves preserve runtime enum values and persisted representations.

## Conventions

Definitions stay beside their implementation unless independent consumers need a neutral contract. Feature contracts belong to the feature and external callers use explicit public entries. Portable UI controls own their structural prop and style types: primitives belong to `client/ui/elements`, package-wide host contracts belong to `client/ui/hosts`, portable platform state belongs to `client/ui/environment`, domain-neutral composition contracts belong to `client/ui/compositions`, generic DOM-action contracts belong to `client/ui/actions`, and visual asset contracts belong with `client/ui/icons`, `client/ui/illustrations`, or `client/ui/branding`. Those contracts must not derive from schema records, DataFn resources, runtime types, application actions, or state interfaces; owning adapters translate domain models at the UI boundary. Keyboard contracts are shared by controls and application shortcuts. Application action contracts belong to client configuration; shared command-host and event contracts belong to `client/shared-state/commands` and `client/shared-state/events`; resource-panel and notification models belong to their named capabilities. Browser ambient declarations live in client/ambient.

Schema owns cross-layer account, subscription, and legacy persistence wire contracts. Shared account contracts must not import client modules. Legacy serialized formats remain distinct from current DataFn records: deriving them from a newer schema would change their accepted shape. Generated AuthFn and DataFn/Drizzle files remain owned by services/account generation scripts and are never manually rewritten. Type-only dependencies use import type; enums used at runtime retain value imports.

The global client/types and shared/types packages are retired, without replacement catch-all packages or compatibility exports. Splits use direct imports to the actual owner. Billing presentation fields remain in surfaces/subscription; wire enums and billing data belong to schema/account. Store interfaces are separated from legacy mutation/filter wire contracts. Markdown validation and responsive text truncation leave shared utilities for their frontend owners.

## Current ownership follow-up

Product menu contracts live in `client/shell/navigation/app-menu.type.ts`. The inventory retains original paths as baseline provenance and updates destinations for current ownership. Portable UI, including both former icon systems, illustrations, and pure branding assets, is consolidated in the `@21n/ui` workspace, and the old elements, components, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, layout, state, and stores workspace aliases are retired. Product-independent cross-capability state, command ports, events, and services use named owners under `client/shared-state`; runtime context, persistent UI preferences, migrations, shell state, and product-aware branding adapters are colocated with their semantic owners. Historical manifest and alias snapshots remain as evidence; `currentPackages` records the 30 current manifests. `@nucleum/client`, `@nucleum/shared-state`, and `@21n/ui` are registered private source workspaces and are not independently publishable builds.

The empty legacy and catch-all client utility workspaces have since been retired; `currentPackages` now records 30 manifests. The current checker validates 383 module dispositions and 198 unchanged runtime enums, plus the explicitly audited retirement of the disconnected shell cache's `CacheKey` enum. No other runtime-enum retirement is exempted.

The following migration checklist and audit evidence describe the TIDY-478 baseline. Current application, navigation, account, file, and command ownership is described in `client-boundaries.md`.

## Execution checklist

- [x] Inventory first-party declarations, imports, packages, aliases, and generated modules.
- [x] Define ownership and migration conventions before edits.
- [x] Complete module colocation and mixed-contract splits.
- [x] Retire global aliases/packages and update all callers.
- [x] Enforce contract ownership and audit schema derivation and exceptions.
- [x] Verify products, services, extensions, shared packages, and relevant workflows.
- [x] Deliver coherent commits and record issue completion.

The inventory records every discovered module, its declarations and consumers, original ownership, and disposition. Locally declared types in implementation modules remain colocated; generated schemas remain generated; explicit type modules are reviewed against their consumers.

## Audit evidence and retained contracts

[type-ownership-inventory.json](type-ownership-inventory.json) records all 383 baseline type modules (1,168 declarations), their consumers and explicit dispositions, all 41 package manifests including nested deployment packages, and 462 exported constants. The baseline is commit `32154c37`; destinations reflect this migration. Embedded types remain beside their implementation. Packages without type declarations were audited for exports and dependencies too. Source aliases are build-time paths; `@nucleum/client` is a private source workspace, not an independently publishable package.

- `schema/account` owns profile and subscription wire data. `EmailParts` has one definition. `IPlan` is an application presentation model. The Apple verification response now has one source in the payment provider.
- `schema/legacy` owns the existing Surreal mutation, query, sync, resource-action and store-data encodings. The store-data enum is shared with query generation; Svelte observable interfaces remain in DataFn. Legacy contracts are not derived from modern database rows because their date unions and projected fields differ.
- `schema/datafn.ts` derives resource names from `nucleumDatafnSchema`; `schema/features.ts` derives resource/relation inputs from `defineSchema`. The installed schema API does not provide a compatible generic record inference helper for legacy UI models. Generated account/AuthFn and DataFn files remain unchanged and are produced by `db:generate` and `datafn:generate`; no authoritative schema changed in this task.
- Client `Resource`, `MetaResource` and `Product` compose schema values with the existing Next overlay. This composition is intentional; backend callers import schema directly. Memory node models include editor projections and legacy serialized dates and remain capability-owned rather than copying generated service database types.
- Native transcription model identifiers (`tiny.en`) and worker model identifiers (`Xenova/whisper-tiny.en`) are different protocols. Both live in runtime/inference, in separate native and worker modules with their original enum values. ImportSource and StepType enums in product import adapters likewise describe different supported inputs. Position types in the PDF annotator and media grid represent different coordinate contracts.
- Keyboard and interaction-mode definitions belong to `client/ui/elements`; package-wide portable host contracts belong to `client/ui/hosts`; resource-panel actions belong to `client/capabilities/resources`. Generic error codes are schema-owned, while user-facing error presentation stays in `client/capabilities/notifications` and application composition. Markdown validation belongs to memory, and responsive truncation belongs to the text primitive; shared utilities no longer import client implementations.
- Existing shared utility tests import the relocated validation/truncation functions directly. Their assertions remain unchanged; moving test ownership can be considered separately. Architecture production-layer rules exclude tests, but retired aliases are forbidden in tests too.
- The legacy relay request contract now lives with its server endpoint in `server/common/relay/relay.type.ts` and imports only schema-owned resource and query contracts. Server-to-client imports have no exceptions.
- Existing frontend implementation cycles are not claimed to be removed. Type-only imports erase type dependencies; runtime composition and feature API reduction remain coordinated with TIDY-477. This issue enforces cross-layer contract ownership and deliberate feature entries, not complete acyclicity of the application.

## Import and export rules

Import interfaces and aliases with `import type` or named `type` specifiers. Runtime enum uses must remain value imports. Do not re-export a moved definition from its former location. Public feature entries are listed in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json` and must match the feature package exports. DataFn and schema expose their new contracts directly. Do not create a new generic types package.

`npm run check:architecture` checks static imports, exports, dynamic imports, import types, CommonJS requires and Vitest mock imports. It rejects production schema/shared/server/service imports into client code, rejects all server-to-client imports, and rejects the retired package aliases. Historical specs and append-only `.conduct` reports retain references to the old layout as historical evidence; active guidance and configuration use the new owners.

## Verification

`npm run check:apps` passes for Nucleum, Memotron, Pointron and Timear with zero errors (379, 302, 308 and 0 warnings respectively). Account-service typechecking passes. The repository unit suite passes 277 tests with 3 skips; Playwright discovers 549 tests in 55 files. Focus session and Markdown persistence browser probes pass on the local HTTPS Nucleum host.

The share extension production build passes. Its check now reports two pre-existing errors instead of 47: unsupported `aria-label` on the debug-log button component and an optional NodeType at the route boundary. The original commit reproduces both. Timear extension build cannot initialize because the installed Sharp native binary is missing. Account memory integration cannot initialize because installed zod-to-json-schema imports an unavailable zod/v3 export; the original commit reproduces this failure. The separate legacy server suite has identical original/current results: 27 failing suites, 2 passing suites, 9 failed tests, 35 passed and 9 skipped. These include removed legacy Flux imports, missing provider dependencies, real-service integration failures and existing assertions. They are not evidence of migration regressions or passing end-to-end coverage.

`node tools/check/type-ownership.mjs` checks all recorded destinations and compares 199 runtime enum declarations to the baseline. `npm run check:architecture`, `npm run check:no-fixed-test-waits`, `npm run check:no-legacy-runtime`, `npm run lint` and the Turbo build graph dry-run pass. Lint has no package lint scripts and runs the configured static build prerequisite; it is not a claim of repository-wide formatting or ESLint coverage. Existing source aliases remain build-time dependencies; they are not indiscriminately added as workspace dependencies, which would create Turbo cycles. Contract consumers use the schema dependency and the existing frontend package/alias model.

Reproduce the browser checks with `node apps/e2e-playwright/scripts/probe-review-session.mjs` and `node apps/e2e-playwright/scripts/probe-markdown-ownership.mjs` while the local product server is running. Neither requires existing user data; each runs in a fresh offline browser context. Full cross-product Playwright, live auth/sync, native app packaging and production deployment were not exercised.

## Historical overlay/resource ownership refinement

TIDY-477 originally moved reusable popup contracts to the then-current elements package, overlay state to the then-current stores workspace, active-resource/selection state to its resource group, and generic ResourceError to DataFn. The current destinations are `client/ui/elements/modal`, `client/application/shell/overlays`, `client/capabilities/resources`, and DataFn respectively. The default error message belongs to `client/capabilities/notifications`. The inventory destinations follow the current owners so baseline enum validation stays reproducible. See client-boundaries.md for the permanent overlay host contract and the remaining application-specific dependencies.

item.stdout: client/composition/README.md # Product composition (@nucleum/composition) This workspace wires independently owned implementations into a running product. It is not the default owner of connected components or workflows. ## Permanent owners - root files: `configure-hosts.ts` registers hosts, `shortcuts.config.ts` supplies product shortcut defaults, `global-commands.ts` and `settings-actions.ts` assemble owner-defined actions, `SubAtomLogo.svelte` connects product identity to portable marks, and `AppLoadingView.svelte` and `ComponentResolver.svelte` connect startup and action presentation. - layers: startup ordering, account access gating, connected user layout assembly, shell overlay mounting and telemetry consent/lifecycle wiring. - chrome: product-connected snippets supplied to the independent shell, including native capture. The root source files are an explicit allowlist in the architecture checker. New root files or directories require an ownership decision and checker update. ## Responsibilities owned elsewhere - shell/navigation and shell/layers: browser navigation, route decoding, route-driven layout, platform classes and viewport handling. - shell/overlays and shell/modal: modal stacking, chrome and dismissal; composition registers the concrete action renderer and mounts the overlay layer. - surfaces/settings and products/pointron/settings: settings action definitions; composition preserves their final registry order. - surfaces/library: mixed-resource rendering and bulk selection presentation; features/records owns record actions and bulk mutations. - surfaces/account: OAuth, session hydration, extension login and environment-change sign-out. - surfaces/subscription: plan reconciliation and native purchase outcomes. - surfaces/settings/data-recovery: recovery decisions and UI; persistence/migrations owns headless import mechanics. - surfaces/settings/about: application-update workflow. - surfaces/help: documentation, support, connected error recovery and shipped diagnostics. - surfaces/sharing: permissions and public-link workflows. - runtime: host detection, native message validation, service workers and log capture. - shared-state/app-context, preferences and files: application metadata, timezone preferences and native file responses. - ui/compositions: quick-access grids, hold-action presentation and point-map rendering. - features/memory/maps: memory popup content and its map adapter. Composition keeps lifecycle sequencing and supplies narrow callbacks to the owning workflows. Do not move a large layer wholesale into another generic controller, service, state or utilities directory. Do not add compatibility re-exports at retired paths. client/features/README.md # `client/features` — user-facing content capabilities (`@nucleum/features`) Charter: the marquee things a user creates and manages. Each feature is a self-contained capability reached from outside only through declared entry points. ## Owners `calendar`, `collections`, `focus`, `memory`, `records`, `spaces`, `system`. ## Belongs here A cohesive content capability with its own UI, state, and logic. `records` owns connected record actions and bulk mutations; shared-state supplies their headless selection state and application-configured host. ## Import rules (enforced) - May import `ui`, `shared-state`, `runtime`, `datafn`, and the application **shell** surface only. - May **not** import `products` or application workflows outside the shell. - Cross-feature imports must target a path declared in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`; there is no barrel. ## Junk-drawer test If the thing operates *across* features or is *about the app itself* — account and billing, the command palette, the resource library/browser, settings, onboarding, help — it is a **product surface** and belongs in the top-level `client/surfaces/` workspace (see `docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md`). `features/` must never import `surfaces/`; the checker rejects that edge. client/runtime/README.md # `client/runtime` — browser infrastructure, no UI Charter: how the client talks to the outside world and computes, with no presentation and no product workflow. It sits at the bottom and may be imported by everyone, including extensions and workers that never load the full app. ## Owners `account` (session state + transport), `audio`, `connectivity`, `embed`, `inference`, `logging`, `os`, `context`. ## Belongs here Transport, network authority, native/embed messaging, inference, audio decoding, diagnostics, and the bare reactive state those need. Pure, low-dependency, changes rarely. ## Never here (enforced) Any import of `features`, `products`, `application`, the shell, `shared-state`, or portable UI. Runtime is a leaf that others depend on, not the reverse. ## Junk-drawer test - Has Svelte/DOM UI? -> not runtime. - Coordinates a user-facing workflow (redirects, screens, prompts)? -> that workflow belongs in `application` or a feature; keep only the primitive here. (Example: `account.store` state lives here; the sign-in workflow does not.) client/shared-state/README.md # `client/shared-state` — product-independent shared client state (`@nucleum/shared-state`) Charter: reactive state and cross-cutting ports consumed across many features, products, extensions, and the application shell. Not UI, not infrastructure, not a single feature's state. Named `shared-state`, **not** `capabilities`: user-facing capabilities are `features/` (and product surfaces). This layer is the state they share. ## Owners (import named subpaths, no root barrel) `app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`, `preferences`, `product`, `resources`, `shortcuts`. `events` owns the focus and memory event contracts; runtime extensions own clipper transport events. `product` exposes the configured presentation host consumed by surfaces without importing application composition. `resources` owns headless resource state and host contracts; connected record actions and bulk mutations live in `features/records`. Example: `@nucleum/shared-state/preferences/preferences.store`. ## Belongs here State or a contract that more than one feature/product needs and that has no UI and no product-specific workflow. Concrete command *execution* stays in application; the command *port* lives here because everyone consumes it. ## Never here (enforced) Any import, direct or transitive, of `application`, `features`, or `products`. May consume `runtime`, `datafn`, `persistence`, `schema`, `utils`, and portable UI contracts only. ## Junk-drawer test client/shell/README.md # `client/shell` — application shell: arrangement and navigation (`@nucleum/shell`) Charter: how the app is arranged and moved through, independent of what content fills it. Pure "where things go and how you move", never "what a screen does". ## Owners `navigation` (URL/history, resource navigation), `topNav`, `bottomNav`, `leftPanel`, `rightPanel`, `trail`, `layers` (theme, metadata, embed), `overlays`, `modal`, `paint` (page and resource resolvers fed through the shared-state action renderer), `split views`, `tabs`, `sync` and `notifications` chrome. `navigation/NavigationLayout.svelte` owns route-driven arrangement and receives connected nav snippets from application. `overlays/ModalLayer.svelte` owns the overlay stack and resolves action content through the registered renderer. ## Belongs here Anything that owns URL state, panel arrangement, tab/sidebar behavior, product menus, or shell events. If removing it would not change what any single screen does, only how screens are framed and reached, it belongs here. ## Not here - Domain screens and workflows (account, library, settings, command) -> `surfaces/`. - Portable domain-free UI -> `ui/`. - Content capabilities -> `features/`. - Sync scheduling -> `datafn/visibility-sync`; telemetry mechanics -> `runtime/telemetry`; consent/lifecycle wiring -> application layers; connected support -> `surfaces/help/support`. - Application composition layers that wire the running product together (base/user layers, the action `ComponentResolver`, `AppLoadingView`, and the final settings action assembly) -> `application/`. client/static/README.md # static Shared static assets package for all product apps. ## Usage ### Basic Import ```javascript import { assets, assetPath } from 'static'; // Use predefined assets const logoSrc = assets.nucleusLogo; const soundFile = assets.sounds.dingding; const iconSrc = assets.icons.arrowBack; // Or construct paths dynamically const customPath = assetPath('my-custom-asset.png'); ``` ### In Svelte Components ```svelte

It is not the default owner of connected components or workflows. ## Permanent owners - root files: `configure-hosts.ts` registers hosts, `shortcuts.config.ts` supplies product shortcut defaults, `global-commands.ts` and `settings-actions.ts` assemble owner-defined actions, `SubAtomLogo.svelte` connects product identity to portable marks, and `AppLoadingView.svelte` and `ComponentResolver.svelte` connect startup and action presentation. - layers: startup ordering, account access gating, connected user layout assembly, shell overlay mounting and telemetry consent/lifecycle wiring. - chrome: product-connected snippets supplied to the independent shell, including native capture. The root source files are an explicit allowlist in the architecture checker. New root files or directories require an ownership decision and checker update. ## Responsibilities owned elsewhere - shell/navigation and shell/layers: browser navigation, route decoding, route-driven layout, platform classes and viewport handling. - shell/overlays and shell/modal: modal stacking, chrome and dismissal; composition registers the concrete action renderer and mounts the overlay layer. - surfaces/settings and products/pointron/settings: settings action definitions; composition preserves their final registry order. - surfaces/library: mixed-resource rendering and bulk selection presentation; features/records owns record actions and bulk mutations. - surfaces/account: OAuth, session hydration, extension login and environment-change sign-out. - surfaces/subscription: plan reconciliation and native purchase outcomes. - surfaces/settings/data-recovery: recovery decisions and UI; persistence/migrations owns headless import mechanics. - surfaces/settings/about: application-update workflow. - surfaces/help: documentation, support, connected error recovery and shipped diagnostics. - surfaces/sharing: permissions and public-link workflows. - runtime: host detection, native message validation, service workers and log capture. - shared-state/app-context, preferences and files: application metadata, timezone preferences and native file responses. - ui/compositions: quick-access grids, hold-action presentation and point-map rendering. - features/memory/maps: memory popup content and its map adapter. Composition keeps lifecycle sequencing and supplies narrow callbacks to the owning workflows. Do not move a large layer wholesale into another generic controller, service, state or utilities directory. Do not add compatibility re-exports at retired paths. client/features/README.md # `client/features` — user-facing content capabilities (`@nucleum/features`) Charter: the marquee things a user creates and manages. Each feature is a self-contained capability reached from outside only through declared entry points. ## Owners `calendar`, `collections`, `focus`, `memory`, `records`, `spaces`, `system`. ## Belongs here A cohesive content capability with its own UI, state, and logic. `records` owns connected record actions and bulk mutations; shared-state supplies their headless selection state and application-configured host. ## Import rules (enforced) - May import `ui`, `shared-state`, `runtime`, `datafn`, and the application **shell** surface only. - May **not** import `products` or application workflows outside the shell. - Cross-feature imports must target a path declared in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`; there is no barrel. ## Junk-drawer test If the thing operates *across* features or is *about the app itself* — account and billing, the command palette, the resource library/browser, settings, onboarding, help — it is a **product surface** and belongs in the top-level `client/surfaces/` workspace (see `docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md`). `features/` must never import `surfaces/`; the checker rejects that edge. client/runtime/README.md # `client/runtime` — browser infrastructure, no UI Charter: how the client talks to the outside world and computes, with no presentation and no product workflow. It sits at the bottom and may be imported by everyone, including extensions and workers that never load the full app. ## Owners `account` (session state + transport), `audio`, `connectivity`, `embed`, `inference`, `logging`, `os`, `context`. ## Belongs here Transport, network authority, native/embed messaging, inference, audio decoding, diagnostics, and the bare reactive state those need. Pure, low-dependency, changes rarely. ## Never here (enforced) Any import of `features`, `products`, `application`, the shell, `shared-state`, or portable UI. Runtime is a leaf that others depend on, not the reverse. ## Junk-drawer test - Has Svelte/DOM UI? -> not runtime. - Coordinates a user-facing workflow (redirects, screens, prompts)? -> that workflow belongs in `application` or a feature; keep only the primitive here. (Example: `account.store` state lives here; the sign-in workflow does not.) client/shared-state/README.md # `client/shared-state` — product-independent shared client state (`@nucleum/shared-state`) Charter: reactive state and cross-cutting ports consumed across many features, products, extensions, and the application shell. Not UI, not infrastructure, not a single feature's state. Named `shared-state`, **not** `capabilities`: user-facing capabilities are `features/` (and product surfaces). This layer is the state they share. ## Owners (import named subpaths, no root barrel) `app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`, `preferences`, `product`, `resources`, `shortcuts`. `events` owns the focus and memory event contracts; runtime extensions own clipper transport events. `product` exposes the configured presentation host consumed by surfaces without importing application composition. `resources` owns headless resource state and host contracts; connected record actions and bulk mutations live in `features/records`. Example: `@nucleum/shared-state/preferences/preferences.store`. ## Belongs here State or a contract that more than one feature/product needs and that has no UI and no product-specific workflow. Concrete command *execution* stays in application; the command *port* lives here because everyone consumes it. ## Never here (enforced) Any import, direct or transitive, of `application`, `features`, or `products`. May consume `runtime`, `datafn`, `persistence`, `schema`, `utils`, and portable UI contracts only. ## Junk-drawer test client/shell/README.md # `client/shell` — application shell: arrangement and navigation (`@nucleum/shell`) Charter: how the app is arranged and moved through, independent of what content fills it. Pure "where things go and how you move", never "what a screen does". ## Owners `navigation` (URL/history, resource navigation), `topNav`, `bottomNav`, `leftPanel`, `rightPanel`, `trail`, `layers` (theme, metadata, embed), `overlays`, `modal`, `paint` (page and resource resolvers fed through the shared-state action renderer), `split views`, `tabs`, `sync` and `notifications` chrome. `navigation/NavigationLayout.svelte` owns route-driven arrangement and receives connected nav snippets from application. `overlays/ModalLayer.svelte` owns the overlay stack and resolves action content through the registered renderer. ## Belongs here Anything that owns URL state, panel arrangement, tab/sidebar behavior, product menus, or shell events. 24	## Ownership
    25	
    26	`schema` owns resource definitions. `client/datafn` owns the client storage and sync runtime. `client/runtime` owns browser infrastructure such as account transport, network authority, connectivity, and diagnostic logging. `client/features` owns capability implementations. `client/products` composes those capabilities into product experiences. Client product identity composition lives in `client/config/product.type.ts`; cross-layer product identity lives in `schema/product.type.ts`; declarative navigation metadata lives in `client/config`.
    27	
    28	`client/ui` is the permanent domain-free `@21n/ui` package. `elements` owns atomic controls and UI-only types. `compositions` owns domain-neutral compound UI intended for present or future reuse, including charts, maps, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, file presentation, keyboard listeners, duration inputs, scroll containers, and time selectors. `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, and `branding` owns pure visual brand assets. Package-wide portable platform state belongs to `environment`, while dependency-inversion contracts shared across controls and compositions belong to `hosts`. A single current consumer does not make a composition feature-owned. `client/shell` (`@nucleum/shell`) owns the concrete product shell: navigation, panels, split views, tabs, trails, overlays, modal chrome, and the extension-support layers. `client/surfaces` (`@nucleum/surfaces`) owns cross-feature product surfaces: account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, the command surface (`commandBar`, `commands`, `search`), and `library` resource browsing. `client/composition` (`@nucleum/composition`) owns the composition root (`configure-hosts.ts`, `shortcuts.config.ts`), the base/user application layers, shell overlay mounting, chrome integration adapters, and product-aware branding adapters. Markdown editing and tags belong to memory; combinations belong to spaces. Product-independent shared client behavior lives in the `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace under explicit `app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`, `preferences`, `product`, `resources`, and `shortcuts` owners. Cross-layer billing contracts live in `schema/account`. Keyboard and interaction-mode contracts live in `client/ui/elements/keyboard`; panel and error presentation contracts live in their capability owners. See [type ownership](type-ownership.md) for the complete inventory.
    29	
    30	## Enforced rules
    31	
    32	Run `npm run check:architecture`. CI and the root lint command run the same check. It resolves relative imports, source aliases, dynamic imports, and TypeScript import types in TypeScript and Svelte scripts.
    33	
    34	- Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition; the top-level shell is the only app-level layer features may consume. Surfaces may compose features; features must never import surfaces.
    35	- Surfaces must not import application composition. Product presentation and action rendering enter surfaces through narrow shared-state hosts installed by application composition.
    36	- The application shell is acyclic: `client/shell` must not import application, surfaces, or products, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters only through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome (brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status, capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props wired by the application chrome adapters (`client/composition/chrome/`).
    37	- Portable UI cannot directly or transitively import application state, runtime, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, or domain state.
    38	- Compositions may use elements, actions, environment, and hosts; those lower UI layers cannot import compositions.
    39	- Shared state cannot directly or transitively import application, feature, or product implementations.
    40	- DataFn and runtime files cannot directly import features, products, application composition or shell, portable UI, or shared client state and services.
    41	- Composition calculations cannot import the session singleton.
    42	- A caller outside a capability must use a source file explicitly listed in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`.
    43	
    44	The feature entry-point list records the existing public surface, including individual components and type modules; it is not a barrel module. Additions require an explicit contract change. Package exports expose these same paths. Source aliases bypass package exports, which is why the source-level check remains necessary.
    45	
    46	## Current architecture contract
    47	
    48	Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition. The application shell is the top-level `client/shell` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`), the only app-level layer features may consume. Cross-feature product surfaces live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`); surfaces may compose features, while features never import surfaces.     49

    53	transport events live under `client/runtime/extensions`. App metadata belongs to
    54	`client/shared-state/app-context`. Surfaces consume application-selected action
    55	rendering and product visuals through named shared-state hosts.
    56	
    57	Presentation ownership is separate from navigation ownership. Sidebars, tabs, split views, panels, and trails remain in the application shell when they own URL state, resource resolution, product menus, shell events, or other application orchestration. A component moves to UI only when its public contract can be expressed without product or domain vocabulary.
    58	
    59	Application and extension shells configure permanent overlay, resource-action, panel, shortcut, recents, record-renderer, action-renderer, portable action, shortcut, file, environment, logging, and haptic contracts in `client/composition/configure-hosts.ts`. Configuration runs from base, user, and extension shells before presentation or command execution. Shell and feature adapters provide view-specific props such as keyboard matching, time scales, and address resolution. Shared Markdown display owns portable parsing; memory owns Markdown editing. Portable file presentation, resource enums, event contracts, and action identifiers no longer depend on capability implementations.
    60	
    61	The public feature API is enumerated in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`. Each has a static consumer outside its capability. The checker rejects unused public entries and private external imports. This reduces the previous 154 entries by moving shared contracts and infrastructure to their proper owners without introducing barrels or compatibility paths.
    62	
    63	Registered workspaces declare their production source imports. `@nucleum/client` owns lower-level config and runtime; `@nucleum/shared-state` owns product-independent shared client behavior, application context, command ports, and events; `@nucleum/shell` owns the application shell; `@nucleum/surfaces` owns cross-feature product surfaces; `@21n/ui` owns all portable presentation and visual assets. Peers describe the host's source compilation requirements without adding artificial Turbo build cycles. This is not a claim that each source package builds or installs independently. The portable UI foundation is the single `client/ui` workspace, consumed through `@21n/ui/elements`, `@21n/ui/compositions`, `@21n/ui/actions`, `@21n/ui/icons`, `@21n/ui/illustrations`, `@21n/ui/branding`, `@21n/ui/environment`, and `@21n/ui/hosts`. Compositions may use the other UI layers, while elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts never depend on compositions. The entire package remains independent, directly and transitively, from application state, runtime infrastructure, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Domain-neutral compositions stay in UI when future shared use is intentional, even with one current consumer. Product-connected behavior enters through explicit props or narrow contracts under `client/ui/hosts`, configured from `client/composition/configure-hosts.ts` or supplied by the owning shell or feature adapter. Shared state and utilities cannot transitively load application or feature composition at runtime. Explicit type-only edges are excluded from the shared-runtime reachability rule; cross-capability imports remain permitted through declared public entries, so the complete source graph is not claimed to be acyclic.
    49	
    50	`client/shared-state` is the single `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace. It groups product-independent Nucleum client behavior by semantic owner without turning `client/` into a list of service folders. Shared command ports and application events are shared state because they are consumed across features, products, extensions, and application composition; concrete command execution remains application-owned. Shared state may consume lower-level runtime, DataFn, persistence, schema, utilities, and portable UI contracts. They may not consume application workflows or shell implementations, user-facing feature implementations, or product composition, directly or transitively. Consumers import named subpaths such as `@nucleum/shared-state/preferences/preferences.store`; there is no root barrel, `shared`, `core`, generic `state`, or nested generic `stores` bucket.
    51	
    52	Focus and memory event contracts live under `client/shared-state/events`; clipper
    53	transport events live under `client/runtime/extensions`. App metadata belongs to
    54	`client/shared-state/app-context`. Surfaces consume application-selected action
    55	rendering and product visuals through named shared-state hosts.
    56	
    57	Presentation ownership is separate from navigation ownership. Neutral breadcrumbs and scroll containers live in UI. `client/shell/navigation/components/AppBreadcrumbs.svelte` translates application resource and path metadata into structural breadcrumb items and callbacks. Sidebars, tabs, split views, panels, and trails remain in the application shell when they own URL state, resource resolution, product menus, shell events, or other application orchestration. A component moves to UI only when its public contract can be expressed without product or domain vocabulary.
    58	
    59	Application and extension shells configure permanent overlay, resource-action, panel, shortcut, recents, record-renderer, action-renderer, portable action, shortcut, file, environment, logging, and haptic contracts in `client/composition/configure-hosts.ts`. Configuration runs from base, user, and extension shells before presentation or command execution. Shell and feature adapters provide view-specific props such as keyboard matching, time scales, and address resolution. Shared Markdown display owns portable parsing; memory owns Markdown editing. Portable file presentation, resource enums, event contracts, and action identifiers no longer depend on capability implementations.
    60	
    61	The public feature API is enumerated in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`. Each has a static consumer outside its capability. The checker rejects unused public entries and private external imports. This reduces the previous 154 entries by moving shared contracts and infrastructure to their proper owners without introducing barrels or compatibility paths.
    62	
    63	Registered workspaces declare their production source imports. `@nucleum/client` owns lower-level config and runtime; `@nucleum/shared-state` owns product-independent shared client behavior, application context, command ports, and events; `@nucleum/shell` owns the application shell; `@nucleum/surfaces` owns cross-feature product surfaces; `@21n/ui` owns all portable presentation and visual assets. Source workspaces bundled by an app declare co-hosted workspace requirements as peer dependencies; existing build dependencies remain dependencies. Peers describe the host's source compilation requirements without adding artificial Turbo build cycles. This is not a claim that each source package builds or installs independently. `client/ambient` contains **TypeScript declarations for APIs that exist outside the app’s modules**. It has no runtime implementation: - [browser-runtime.d.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/ambient/browser-runtime.d.ts) describes the Chrome extension runtime, storage, tabs, and `window.chrome`. - [third-party.d.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/ambient/third-party.d.ts) describes CryptoJS, Instagram embeds, native configuration on `window`, and types for three external packages. - [youtube.d.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/ambient/youtube.d.ts) describes the YouTube player globals. The app TypeScript configs include these declarations. `ambient` is a reasonable name for this bounded purpose; ordinary app types and workflows should stay with their owners. The [type ownership guide](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/docs/architecture/type-ownership.md:7) says the same. **There is no maintained visual dependency map in the architecture docs.** The current references are the prose [client boundaries guide](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:24) and the executable [architecture checker](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/tools/check/architecture.mjs:331). Here is a simplified map; arrows mean “may consume,” not “must import”: ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Apps, routes, extensions"] --> B["Products and composition
product setup and final wiring"] B --> C["Surfaces
account, settings, library, commands"] B --> D["Features
memory, focus, records, etc."] C --> D C --> E["Shell
navigation, panels, overlays"] D --> E C --> F["Shared state
named state and host contracts"] D --> F E --> F F --> G["Runtime, DataFn, persistence, schema"] C --> H["UI
portable presentation"] D --> H E --> H H --> I["Theme and shared utilities"] ``` The key restrictions are: `ui` cannot reach product or domain code; `shared-state` cannot reach features, surfaces, shell, products, or composition; features cannot reach surfaces, products, or composition; shell cannot reach surfaces, products, or composition; surfaces cannot reach composition. `runtime` and `datafn` cannot reach the higher UI and workflow layers. `config`, `static`, and `theme` supply identifiers, assets, and presentation foundations; `next/noop` is a small empty Next-product overlay. `ambient` sits outside the runtime import graph. This is an **ownership overview**, not a complete dependency DAG. Products and surfaces currently reference one another in source, and the checker enforces specific forbidden edges rather than a single exhaustive “may import” matrix. No files were changed.

portable presentation"] D --> H E --> H H --> I["Theme and shared utilities"] ``` The key restrictions are: `ui` cannot reach product or domain code; `shared-state` cannot reach features, surfaces, shell, products, or composition; features cannot reach surfaces, products, or composition; shell cannot reach surfaces, products, or composition; surfaces cannot reach composition. `runtime` and `datafn` cannot reach the higher UI and workflow layers. `config`, `static`, and `theme` supply identifiers, assets, and presentation foundations; `next/noop` is a small empty Next-product overlay. `ambient` sits outside the runtime import graph. This is an **ownership overview**, not a complete dependency DAG. Products and surfaces currently reference one another in source, and the checker enforces specific forbidden edges rather than a single exhaustive “may import” matrix. No files were changed.

# Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.

If explicit user input is required for another reason before progress can safely continue, do not use the `request_user_input` tool. Ask the user directly with one concise plain-text question instead. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.

If explicit user input is required for another reason before progress can safely continue, do not use the `request_user_input` tool. Ask the user directly with one concise plain-text question instead. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.

docs/architecture/type-ownership.md:42:- Keyboard and interaction-mode definitions belong to `client/ui/elements`; package-wide portable host contracts belong to `client/ui/hosts`; resource-panel actions belong to `client/capabilities/resources`. Generic error codes are schema-owned, while user-facing error presentation stays in `client/capabilities/notifications` and application composition. Markdown validation belongs to memory, and responsive truncation belongs to the text primitive; shared utilities no longer import client implementations.
docs/architecture/type-ownership.md:65:TIDY-477 originally moved reusable popup contracts to the then-current elements package, overlay state to the then-current stores workspace, active-resource/selection state to its resource group, and generic ResourceError to DataFn. The current destinations are `client/ui/elements/modal`, `client/application/shell/overlays`, `client/capabilities/resources`, and DataFn respectively. The default error message belongs to `client/capabilities/notifications`. The inventory destinations follow the current owners so baseline enum validation stays reproducible. See client-boundaries.md for the permanent overlay host contract and the remaining application-specific dependencies.
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:77:The former `client/stores`, `client/state`, `client/commands`, and `client/events` directories are retired. App context, appearance, commands, events, files, notifications, preferences, resources, and shortcuts have explicit owners under `client/shared-state`. Runtime environment state belongs to runtime, migration state belongs to persistence, the observable-store implementation belongs to DataFn, and overlay state belongs to the application shell. New state follows semantic ownership and must not recreate a catch-all `stores`, `state`, `shared`, or `core` directory; `client/shared-state` is the single approved shared-state workspace and keeps named owners with no root barrel.
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:241:Cross-feature product surfaces (account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, command, search, and library) live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`). Surfaces may compose features, shell, shared state, runtime, and products; features must never import surfaces. The former `client/application` workspace is retired. Its remaining composition responsibilities live in `client/composition`, with explicit root files, `layers/`, and `chrome/`.
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:310:The overlay store now lives in `client/stores/overlays` and owns modal, mini-player and fullscreen state without importing application navigation. `appStore` configures its `OverlayHost` once during module initialization; callbacks preserve dismissal events, fullscreen URL parameters and associated-player selection. This is the permanent shell contract, with an explicit error if a caller uses an overlay without a configured shell. Architecture enforcement rejects transitive overlay dependencies on application, feature or product implementations.
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:312:At this phase, reusable modal header/footer/padding and popup props moved to `client/elements/modal`, selection and active-resource stores moved to `client/stores/resources`, and resource grid/star/trash feedback moved to the then-shared `client/components/records` owner. The current contract above supersedes that interim location: connected record presentation now lives in `client/features/records`. Generic resource errors and read-only lookup belong to DataFn; the file capability owns the existing upload limit. Application mutation orchestration and feature-composed record rendering remained in application at this phase. The retired-path registry prevents old locations from returning.
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:327:ResourceActions and BulkEditor now live in `client/stores/resources`. The composing appStore supplies ResourceActionHost for navigation, tabs, link dialogs, clipboard links and awaited node lifecycle hooks. This removes the ResourceActions -> BulkEditor -> node.store -> ResourceActions dependency cycle. Thumbnail presentation no longer imports resource stores to choose menus: node, collection, objective and task callers supply their resolver with the same access-point parameters. Unsupported event and combination menus remain empty.
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:341:At this phase, panel enums, URL resolution and panel state transitions moved to `client/stores/resources`, while reusable panel presentation moved to the interim `client/components/records` owner. The current contract above supersedes that location: the connected panel presentation now lives in `client/features/records`. ResourcePanelHost supplies shell navigation. Callers pass the current SvelteKit URL explicitly when resolving the panel, keeping the shell store independent of SvelteKit page-store initialization. URL suffixes and values, default/focus toggles, update/event ordering and navigation semantics are preserved. The previous application and component paths are retired.
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:380:Reusable shortcut persistence/matching lives in `client/stores/keyboard`; the component listener lives in `client/components/keyboard` and formatting/modifier utilities in `client/elements/keyboard`. ShortcutHost supplies application defaults and current product-configurable actions from the app shell. The original DataFn resource, merge/load behavior, Windows default modifier mapping, exact matching and text-input handling are preserved. The application shortcut runner and default command configuration remain application-owned. Direct dependencies from the shared shortcut store/listener into application or product implementations are rejected; this does not claim all broader store dependencies are transitively isolated.
docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:393:Recent-record state now lives in `client/stores/resources/recent.store.ts`, with its state contract in `recent.type.ts`. The shell configures RecentsHost to read the current app product whenever an everything query runs. Explicit resource refreshes retain their existing behavior. The state key, query limits, archive/trash filters, date normalization, typed exclusions, ordering, duplicate replacement and partial-failure handling are unchanged. The unused memory-node import is removed. Direct imports into application, feature or product implementations and the app store are rejected from the recent-record modules. Broader transitive store dependencies remain outside this phase's enforcement.

AGENTS.md:7:Agents MUST confirm the active product context before touching UI or workflow code. They MUST inspect `client/products/*` configurations and the app context exposed from `client/shared-state/app-context` to respect feature gates and product-specific behaviors. Rationale: enforcing product awareness prevents regressions across Nucleus, Memotron, Pointron, and future bundles.
AGENTS.md:33:  - `client/shared-state/`: Product-independent shared Nucleum client state (`@nucleum/shared-state`) grouped by semantic owner, including app context, appearance, commands, events, files, notifications, preferences, resources, and shortcuts.
AGENTS.md:58:- Application-wide context belongs to the named `client/shared-state/app-context` owner. Shared command ports and application-event contracts belong in `client/shared-state/commands` and `client/shared-state/events`; command execution infrastructure lives in `client/surfaces/commands`, action definitions stay with their semantic owners, and final registry assembly lives at the `client/composition` root. Runtime environment state belongs in `client/runtime`, persisted UI preference state belongs in `client/shared-state/preferences`, and migration helpers belong in `client/persistence/migrations`. The generic `client/state`, standalone `client/commands`, `client/events`, `client/layout`, `client/branding`, `client/illustrations`, `client/icons`, and `client/iconsV2` directories and their aliases are permanently retired.
AGENTS.md:60:- Do not create a new catch-all `stores`, `state`, `shared`, or `core` directory. The `client/shared-state` workspace is the single approved home for product-independent shared client state and MUST keep named owners with no root barrel or generic dumping at its root. Colocate feature and domain state with its semantic owner. Product-independent client behavior shared by multiple features or products belongs to a named owner under `client/shared-state`, never directly in the shared-state root.
AGENTS.md:61:- `@nucleum/shared-state` may depend on lower-level runtime, DataFn, persistence, schema, and portable UI contracts, but MUST NOT depend directly or transitively on application, feature, or product implementations. Features, the shell, products, and application composition may consume explicit shared-state subpaths. Do not add a shared-state root barrel.
AGENTS.md:62:- Account state must not own file processing, deletion confirmation, or subscription workflows. Shared uploads belong in `client/shared-state/files`, and user workflows belong in `client/surfaces/account` or `client/surfaces/subscription`.
AGENTS.md:63:- Keep generic UI-state persistence in `client/shared-state/preferences`; tabs, sidebar behavior, and product menu customization belong with the application shell. Headless notification and shortcut state belongs in shared-state. Connected notification rendering and global shortcut execution belong under `client/shell`; shortcut settings presentation belongs under `client/surfaces/settings/shortcuts`. The former `client/application/notifications` and `client/application/shortcuts` paths remain retired; do not recreate them under `client/composition`. Focus owns its scheduled notifications; runtime owns native message delivery.
AGENTS.md:213:- Added the narrow product navigation config host (`client/shared-state/product/product-config-host`, registered from `resource-hosts.ts`) as the only product data the shell reads.
AGENTS.md:219:- Relocated `resolveTrialDaysLeft` to `client/runtime/account/plan.utils` and the library resource predicates to `client/shared-state/resources/library.utils`, removing the remaining shell imports of features and subscription surfaces.
AGENTS.md:223:- Renamed the shared client state workspace from `client/capabilities` to `client/shared-state` (`@nucleum/shared-state`), approving that name as the single shared-state home while retaining the named-owner and no-root-barrel rules.

AGENTS.md:58:- Application-wide context belongs to the named `client/shared-state/app-context` owner. Shared command ports and application-event contracts belong in `client/shared-state/commands` and `client/shared-state/events`; command execution infrastructure lives in `client/surfaces/commands`, action definitions stay with their semantic owners, and final registry assembly lives at the `client/composition` root. Runtime environment state belongs in `client/runtime`, persisted UI preference state belongs in `client/shared-state/preferences`, and migration helpers belong in `client/persistence/migrations`. The generic `client/state`, standalone `client/commands`, `client/events`, `client/layout`, `client/branding`, `client/illustrations`, `client/icons`, and `client/iconsV2` directories and their aliases are permanently retired.
AGENTS.md:60:- Do not create a new catch-all `stores`, `state`, `shared`, or `core` directory. The `client/shared-state` workspace is the single approved home for product-independent shared client state and MUST keep named owners with no root barrel or generic dumping at its root. Colocate feature and domain state with its semantic owner. Product-independent client behavior shared by multiple features or products belongs to a named owner under `client/shared-state`, never directly in the shared-state root.
AGENTS.md:61:- `@nucleum/shared-state` may depend on lower-level runtime, DataFn, persistence, schema, and portable UI contracts, but MUST NOT depend directly or transitively on application, feature, or product implementations. Features, the shell, products, and application composition may consume explicit shared-state subpaths. Do not add a shared-state root barrel.
AGENTS.md:62:- Account state must not own file processing, deletion confirmation, or subscription workflows. Shared uploads belong in `client/shared-state/files`, and user workflows belong in `client/surfaces/account` or `client/surfaces/subscription`.
AGENTS.md:63:- Keep generic UI-state persistence in `client/shared-state/preferences`; tabs, sidebar behavior, and product menu customization belong with the application shell. Headless notification and shortcut state belongs in shared-state. # Repository guide

`AGENTS.md` is the governing agent policy. Read it before changes. The current architecture is documented in [client boundaries](docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md) and [type ownership](docs/architecture/type-ownership.md).

## Organization

- `schema/`: cross-layer product/resource definitions, wire contracts, and legacy serialization contracts.
- `client/datafn/`: client storage, queries, sync, and DataFn resource adapters.
- `client/runtime/`: UI-independent auth/account transport, connectivity, logging, native messaging, audio, and inference.
- `client/features/`: shared capabilities such as memory, focus, calendar, collections, and spaces.
- `client/products/`: product-specific composition, configuration, and integrations.
- `client/config/`: client product identity, navigation metadata, and command identifiers.
- `client/composition/`: composition, lifecycle orchestration, chrome/branding adapters, and startup/action rendering.
- `client/surfaces/`: account, subscription, settings, help, sharing, command and library workflows.
- `client/shell/`: navigation, panels, tabs, modal chrome, viewport behavior and connected shell presentation.
- `client/ui/`: the domain-free `@21n/ui` package. Import atomic controls from `@21n/ui/elements`, reusable compound UI from `@21n/ui/compositions`, generic DOM behavior from `@21n/ui/actions`, portable icons from `@21n/ui/icons`, illustrations from `@21n/ui/illustrations`, pure visual brand assets from `@21n/ui/branding`, portable platform state from `@21n/ui/environment`, and host contracts from `@21n/ui/hosts`.
- `client/shared-state/`: the product-independent `@nucleum/shared-state` package with named app-context, appearance, commands, events, files, notifications, preferences, resources, and shortcuts owners.
- `client/persistence/`: persistence helpers and legacy backup/recovery boundaries.
- `services/account/`: AuthFn/DataFn account service, database mappings, lookup integrations, and Node/Worker deployments.
- `shared/`: cross-layer utilities and remaining legacy database objects.
- `apps/`, `extensions/`: deployable product and extension bundles; `apps/e2e-playwright` owns browser verification.

There is no global `client/types`, `shared/types`, or `client/utils` package. Helpers and tests follow their semantic owners; `@21n/utils` is retired. Import contracts from their domain owner. The unused `@nucleum/cx` workspace is retired.

## Composition rules

App context does not implement navigation or command execution. Shared state exposes the command port; `client/surfaces/commands` executes commands whose definitions live with their semantic owners and whose ordered registry is assembled in application composition. The application shell changes URL/history and owns connected notification rendering plus global shortcut execution. Shortcut settings presentation belongs under `client/surfaces/settings/shortcuts`. Application and extension shells install command, overlay, resource, renderer, shortcut, recents, icon-asset, and UI-environment hosts through `client/composition/configure-hosts.ts` before mounting consumers.

Compositions may use elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts; those lower UI layers must not depend on compositions. Nothing under `client/ui` may directly or transitively depend on application state, runtime, shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, or domain state. Supply connected behavior through props or narrow host contracts and keep the adapter with its application, shell, or feature owner. Product-aware branding is an application adapter over portable brand assets. Do not move a domain-neutral composition merely because it currently has only one consumer. A portable-looking renderer such as breadcrumbs belongs in UI; route and resource resolution remain in a shell adapter.

Capabilities may depend on lower-level runtime, DataFn, persistence, schema, and portable UI contracts, but never on application, feature, or product implementations. Add only named capability directories and explicit subpath imports; do not add a capabilities barrel or generic `shared`, `core`, `state`, or `stores` bucket.

Use direct imports after moves, without compatibility wrappers. Shared runtime code must not transitively load capability or application implementations. Features use declared public entries when consuming another capability. Source aliases do not enforce package exports, so run the architecture checker.

## Commands

Run commands from the repository root using npm workspaces and Turbo:

```sh
npm ci --legacy-peer-deps
npm run dev:nucleus
npm run dev:memotron
npm run dev:pointron
npm run check:architecture
node tools/check/type-ownership.mjs
npm run check:apps
npm --workspace @21n/account-service run typecheck
npm run test
npm run lint
npm run build:nucleus
npm run build:memotron-share
```

Use the Caddy HTTPS hosts and account-service health checks in `AGENTS.md` for local browser work. Run one product server and browser worker at a time when practical. Do not treat compiler success as browser, cloud, native-device, or deployment proof.

## Database changes

Regenerate DataFn mappings with the account-service scripts. Generate and commit a forward migration for physical schema changes; never edit an applied migration. Deployment executes the checked-in migration journal. A successful local `datafn:push:local` does not prove that deployment migrations are complete.

## Review and delivery

Preserve unrelated checkout changes. Review product configuration and callers before editing. Follow the existing-test and user-facing behavior approval rules in `AGENTS.md`. Keep code free of inline comments and document exported APIs with JSDoc. PR descriptions must identify changed behavior, relevant verification, and unverified environments.
